His very complexities bent inward, as if his existence was obeying a command greater than itself.
He twisted.
Screamed.
Then shrunk.
Collapsing in on himself in a swirl of violet and gold before...
HUUM!
A glimmering Treasure Cache hovered where he’d once knelt, softly spinning.
Originus Venerant...dead!
Silence fell.
No words.
No movement.
Just stunned, raw silence.
Master Etheopa’s mouth trembled.
Kalysta held her breath.
Then, quietly... she smiled with a sighing sense of sorrow as she thought of those killed by Hannibal.
She held a broken, trembling smile that shook her chest with uneven breath.
Master Tan had been avenged.
And even as she had such a thought, Noah spoke again.
"Don’t run."
The words sounded casual.
Almost lazy.
But they echoed like a blade!
The figures who had arrived glanced about uncertainly.
Who was he referring to?
They didn’t wait long for the answer.
WOOSH!
Torus, the Master of Existence from the Mannafolds, darted across the sky in a bolt of white-blue light, his body streaking toward one of the dormant Inevitabilities in the distance.
Inevitabilities!
He could target them and wake them to cause unfathomable chaos!
It would open up possibilities!
Yet towards this action...
Noah simply shook his head.
The Glyph of the Protagonist pulsed once- purple gold.
A ribbon of golden light shot out and wrapped around Torus.
And...
He disappeared.
And reappeared in the exact same place he’d just been standing seconds ago, his face twisted in disbelief.
Torus roared and surged again.
And thr Glyph of the Protagonist simply flashed again!
WAP!
Back.
Again.
Back.
And again!
The cycle repeated like a cruel joke.
Time rewound for him alone.
The sequence playing endlessly as if the Labyrinth itself refused to let him escape.
As if Origin itself was returning him there constantly!
Noah’s eyes narrowed slightly with terrifying command.
"Stop that."
HUUM!
He lifted a hand.
It descended like judgment.
A golden palm of illusory brilliance smashed down from above, layered with Living Origin Authority.
It struck Torus cleanly, slamming him into the frozen land with a thunderous crack, fissures spreading from the point of impact.
Torus coughed blood.
His blue mana suit cracked and crumbled, shards of protective resonance peeling off him in flakes.
His face twisted as he stared up.
And Noah floated downward, quiet and unhurried, until he stood above the crumpled figure.
"If you repeat something after me," Noah said, calm as always, "you might just live."
Gasps rippled through the crowd.
Kalysta’s mouth fell open.
Sigrid’s brows lifted faintly, her golden eyes unreadable.
Even the fresh Masters of Existence hesitated.
Their minds struggling to grasp what they were witnessing.
Did he not just say those same words to another Master of Existence, Hannibal, And then just killed him?!

chapters.title: Chapter 3889: Repeat after me! II
paragraphs: The Master of the Mannafolds trembled beneath the frozen bark of a glacial Yggdrasil branch, the cold air of the domain wrapping around his form like chains of judgment. His lips were stained crimson. His pride was splintered and dangling, like the cracked mana runes floating around his battered form.
"I have the Mannafolds behind me! A Tower Master in our ranks with a terrifying progression in their Tower of Origin!"
WAA!
Torus, the Mannafolds Master, bared his teeth.
"The Tower Masters of the Mannafolds will hear of this. They will raze your beginning if you do this. They...!"
"Are they here?" Noah asked.
The cold question cut across his fury.
A Tower Master.
An extrenely accomplished Originus Venerant entity! But...were they here?
Torus faltered. "...No."

Noah tilted his head slightly, a faint breath curling from his lips like drifting mist. "Then they definitely won’t be able to save you. Maybe they’ll avenge you. But if you’re dead..." His eyes slowly narrowed, "Do you really care about vengeance?"
"So," Noah finished. "Repeat after me, and I might just let you live."
Something loosened inside Noah’s chest as he said this.
Freedom.

The ability to act as he wished. To speak as he wished. Whether the audience was a Fold Dweller, Living Origin, or Early Creature, it didn’t matter. He didn’t want to bend himself for them. Not anymore.
He wanted to live freely, tyrannically!
Quintessentially!
Torus clenched his jaw. "You killed Hannibal after he said your words," he hissed. "Will you not simply do the same to me?"
Noah’s gaze turned sharp. "I told Hannibal I may let him live. I’m also telling you, I may let you live. Statistically, you have better chances than he did. So I’ll ask again."
He paused.
"Will you repeat after me?"
Silence stretched. A soundless storm of shame and rage twisted in Torus’ eyes. He was a Master of Existence. An Originus Venerant. To speak such words...!
"I will repeat," he spat, venomously.
Noah nodded, the frost near his feet deepening into pale white ice.
"Good. Let’s begin."
He didn’t shout. The words weren’t loud, but they weighed more than mountains.
"Repeat after me," Noah said calmly, "I am a big sack of shit."
Torus flinched. His lips curled back in fury.
"I..." He closed his eyes.
"I am a big sack of shit."
It came out like gravel dragged across his throat.
Noah’s gaze remained impassive. "Next...I disgraced the idea of Mana."
A slight tremble ran through Torus’ shoulders.
"I disgraced the idea of Mana."
Noah nodded coldly and continued!
"I am the disappointment my Folds always feared."
"I...am the disappointment my Folds always feared!"
Each one dragged itself through Torus’ voice like barbed wire. But he said them.
And then...
Noah’s voice dropped.
"One more."
He stepped forward, the glacial wind sweeping his robe in slow waves.
"Repeat after me..." he said. "My eons of cultivation are worthless, and I should just die."
A silence louder than thunder followed.
Torus looked up.
His red-rimmed eyes flickered with fury.
His lips parted, but no words came.
The defiance returned suddenly, violently. "No," Torus roared. "I will not say that! You’re going to kill me anyway, just like Hannibal! I am not saying that!"
Noah tilted his head gently.
"You won’t repeat?"
"I won’t!"
"You won’t repeat?!"
"I fucking wont!"
HUUM!
Noah’s eyes squinted sharply.
"Okay."
There was no anger in his voice. Just finality.
The Glyph of the Protagonist flared once more.
Torus didn’t even have time to scream. His body twisted. Folded. Collapsed into itself like a page being turned. His screams were silent. His resistance meaningless.
A single flash of purple-gold, and he was gone.
In his place, a Treasure Cache shimmered quietly. And then, that too, disappeared.
Another Master of Existence, erased.
A heavy silence fell over the glacial domain.
Sigrid was calmly watching behind Noah. Kalysta and others of the Veiled Sunfolds were astonished as this was far too surreal!
And at this time...
"Fellow Master of Existence," a new voice rang out, strong but tempered, "you cannot just go on killing like this."
The air itself seemed to pause, as a figure stepped forward from the distance, flanked by nine other glowing titans of power.
White robes, embroidered with sigils of balance and retribution. Behind him, dozens of Primarchs hovered solemnly.
"Existence," the voice continued, "preaches harmony and law. If those two were in the wrong, they could have paid. Killing should be the last resort."
Noah’s eyes flicked upward and gazed at the origin of this voice, words quickly blooming to identify him!
|Master Neinoro|:: An Originus Venerant entity from the Lesser Law Folds with approximately 11,134,666 Complexity Quotient and Purity Quotient.
Someone exceeding 10 Million CQ and PQ!
His gaze swept the space, and saw more of them now.
Not from the Nullvein Gravewake Folds, but from outside. Far outside.
In another direction, there stood a being whose skin shimmered with crystalline brilliance, a lattice of light dancing around him. His name pulsed in Noah’s vision.
|Master Lumerion of Geneva Bright Folds|
His arms folded behind his back, and twelve golden circuits whirred like layered halos above his crown.
In another direction, a woman hovered upon swirling flames, her eyes of sapphire and her body clad in robes of thunder. She carried a staff pulsing with every element known!
|Master Oravella of the Radiant Elemental Folds|
She gave Noah a glance both curious and cautious.
And then, there was a tall being with feathers of white and violet, a birdlike mask covering his face. Ethereal energy billowed around him as if he were half-spirit.
|Master Sil’vair of the Spirifolds|
Each led their own parties. Each carried an air of ancient power and mystery.
They affirmed easily that this Labyrinth...had gateways from other locations! Other Folds unfathomably far from the Nullvein Gravewake Folds!
Noah observed them all.
And then, finally, his gaze rested back on Master Neinoro.
He did not argue. Did not shout. He simply... shook his head.
"I’m not interested in trading philosophies on killing," he said.
The glacial frost whispered around him as he turned, walking toward Sigrid.

She stood beside Kalysta, who was still healing, her aura faintly golden with blooming Kismet. Behind them, Master Etheopa and the other Primarchs of the Veiled Sunfolds gazed at Noah with silent awe.
Their expressions said it all.
He had come into their despair and shifted the very current of their destinies.
He did not do it for their awe or thanks.
He did it because he could.
Because he chose to.
And he would continue to choose freely as he turned his head to the Inevitabilities- the Imitation Mutated Inevitabilities that could provide imitations of Everything!

chapters.title: Chapter 3890: Resolve yourself! I
paragraphs: The cold winds stirred gently across the white sea of frost.
Noah stood in its heart, surrounded by the gnarled and stretching branches of the four massive Yggdrasil Trees, their trunks converging like the ancient fingers of fate.

Above and below, the glacial expanse shimmered like cracked crystal, each breath of wind biting with the clarity of silence before a storm as the Masters of Existence from other Folds stirred with caution!
And how could they not be cautious?!
Because across all this silence, Noah’s presence swelled.

He rose slowly into the air, a golden resonance wrapping around his form in coils of silent dominance. The domain stirred. Beneath him, the wriggling masses of the Imitation Mutated Inevitabilities seemed to twitch in anticipation.

Like they knew that they were about to be stirred awake. And the golems that once hovered in still formation began to hum, the runes carved into their frames flickering with warning as they also got ready.
Noah’s will alone had begun to awaken this frozen graveyard as he floated closer and clother to where Inevitabilities and Golems were clustered!
Then, of course, came the voice.
"Fellow Master of Existence," came the silky tone, too smooth to be sincere, "perhaps we can speak now."
Noah did not look toward the voice.
But Master Neinoro stepped forward regardless, white robes swaying behind him, a glint in his eyes that tried to pass for reason.

"With the convergence of paths within the Labyrinth," Neinoro said with a smile that was far too carefully measured, "and despite the... tumultuous encounters, now is an opportune time to coordinate. To introduce ourselves properly, and plan."
He gestured around at the gathering masses. More than a hundred Masters of Existence. Hundreds of Primarchs.

"Surely you sense it?" Neinoro continued. "This is the precipice. The final trial before we are accepted into the Transcendent Folds as those who can stand against the rising Inevitabilities. Why not collaborate? Clear these... beasts together. Divide the fruits accordingly. We, of the Lesser Law Folds, would love to cooperate with others..."
He glanced around, eyes quietly collecting affirmations. A few nodded. Some murmured assent. Others simply watched, waiting for Noah’s answer.
Then Neinoro turned back, expression careful. "You’re powerful, of course. But power isn’t everything. A collective of power with everyone here will be much more helpful in clea-"
"Are you trying your best to die today?" Noah asked quietly.
HUUM!
The words weren’t loud. They were not shouted.
But they silenced Existence!
Master Neinoro’s expression hardened. Behind him, the Masters of Existence stirred.

"Do you truly think," Neinoro said with sharper tone, "that the Foldless Ones who oversee this Labyrinth would let you continue like this? To slaughter unchecked? To move so brazenly? You flaunt your strength now, but there are limits. Everything and everyone...has limits."
Noah didn’t pause in his ascent.
His gaze turned toward the center of the converging trees, where the Inevitabilities writhed, and the ancient golems hovered like titans waiting for command.
He spoke as his Glyph pulsed.
"Then you can be the test," he said softly. "Let’s find out together if I can be stopped."
Neinoro didn’t answer.
Existence answered for him.
Because in that moment, the Glyph of the Protagonist blazed.
It radiated golden light in waves that bent the air and carved silence into the bones of all who stood nearby.
The glacial air thickened. The space near the Inevitabilities twisted. One by one, the wriggling masses began to move as they were awaken by the golden light!
Hundreds of eyes opened across each grotesque creature!
WUUU!
WUU!
WU!
Screams echoed across the sea of frost- alien, primal, and loud enough to shake the boughs of the trees above.
The Inevitabilities had awoken.
Noah remained still.
From behind him, after her work healing Kalysta and others was finished, Sigrid floated quietly to his side.
Her voice brushed against him calmly.
"You want what lies within the Inevitabilities?" she asked gently.
He turned, eyes meeting hers as he thought of Imitated Everything. "Yes."
She followed his gaze to the masses of writhing chaos and the cautious Masters of Existence retreating ever so slightly along the perimeter.
The Inevitabilities moved now with purpose. Heatless frost cracked beneath them, glowing sigils of doom swirling over their bodies. Chaos embodied. And yet...
Sigrid sighed.
"I truly just wanted a bit more time," she whispered, "to be with you before all the complex things unfold..." Her lips curled sadly.
"But this convergence defeats that hope. So..." She stepped forward, brushing the snow-slick wind with her palm. "Is it okay if I help you clean it all up?"
Noah raised his brows slightly, then smiled.
"Go ahead."
She smiled in return. And then...
Brilliance unfolded from her.
Her form pulsed. Not with Origin, not with Paradox, not with Law.
It was something quieter. Something that has been gone for quite dome time!
The brilliance unfurled slowly. White light that wasn’t just light- it was command, sculpted into bloom.
Her feet hovered above the ground, her eyes closed as the glow surged.
She breathed out, and said simply.
"Resolve your discrepancy."
HUUM!
Another breath.
"Resolve your inevitability."
There was no shout. No gesture of battle. Just the stillness of control.
Above every Inevitability and golem...white lotuses bloomed.
Petals of precision. Petals of purpose.
They hung in the air like suspended verdicts.
But a moment after they bloomed...
Screams.
Horrified, wailing, enraged screams.
The Inevitabilities, for all their unnatural complexity and mutated evolution, recoiled in terror. They thrashed. They contorted. But the lotuses, Order...had already taken root.
Flames of purity ignited upon their surfaces.
Their wriggling masses burst into white fire.
The screaming crescendoed!
Dozens burned!
The flames refined. They erased everything unneeded. Everything chaotic!
Even the most terrifying of golems cracked, white lotuses blooming through their cores as if they had always belonged there.
Noah watched silently.
He watched as chaos was devoured by purpose.
As complexity bowed to command.
And in that moment, he understood.
Order did not scream or rage.
It whispered.
And when it whispered, even inevitabilities listened.
Because Order did not beg for obedience.
It simply gave it a path to follow.
And if there was no path?
Then it carved one!
With white lotuses and burning grace as at this moment, a wonder of the Living Origins expressed herself!

chapters.title: Chapter 3891: Resolve yourself! II
paragraphs: The frost still clung to the bones of the glacial domain, though the howls of Inevitabilities died rapidly!
Where once roared chaos and consumption, now only a roaring silence reigned. The wriggling masses, all of them, were burning. The radiant petals of Order had flared... and then all had collapsed.
Inevitabilities ate and ate until they could eat no more.
That was their nature.
Feed them infinite reserves, overwhelm their paradoxical nature, and they would collapse under the very concept they sought to embody.
They were unstable. Even the genuine ones.
True Inevitabilities, those dreadful echoes of contradiction from beyond, were the nightmare of Foldless Ones. The kind that never ceased, never reasoned. Only consumed.
But these? These were imitations. Mutated. Crafted to simulate dread, but not sustain it.
At the end of the day, they were Imitation Mutated Inevitabilities!
That alone was enough for one to ask...how did Living Existences manufacture such creatures? But that was a wonder for another time.
The critical thing now was that these were just imitations.
Against the grinding, unbending light of Order...they were nothing.

Noah floated in the thinning light, breath steady in his chest. Around him, dozens of Masters of Existence hovered cautiously in the frost-rimed distance, hundreds of Primarchs behind them, all murmuring in hushed awe.
The snow had quieted. Only the crystalline groaning of the massive trees of Yggdrasil continued to echo across the sea.
And in the center of it all stood her.
Sigrid.
Her form gleamed with an undeniable authority now- an Authority that wrapped around her like a flowing mantle spun from the threads of law itself.

Her skin radiated a cool white brilliance, her hair adrift in still wind. Her feet did not touch the frost, but the frost itself seemed to reach up toward her as if it sought to cradle her brilliance!
Noah’s gaze didn’t leave her.
There was a sense of careful wonder in his gaze.
Because as he watched the shimmering white lotuses fade into starlight, he realized, truly realized, that Sigrid might be something far beyond what even she believed herself to be.
Her entire lineage had died to fill a hole in her being. And from that hole...something ancient had bloomed.
A lost Authority.
An existential flame of balance and sovereignty. Living Order.
If she was its vessel...
If she wasn’t simply touched by it, but was it...
Then Sigrid might not just be a Living Order.
She might stand the chance to be THE Living Order. Maybe. In a far distant future!
Noah’s eyes narrowed with solemn clarity.
Such a concept would be enough to drive Living Origins mad. Enough to drive entire Civilizations to betray each other.
How would the Living Paradoxes react if they knew? Hell, how would the other Living Existences react?
She gleamed like judgment itself as she opened her lips and uttered a single word.
"Order."
The sound settled.
Like snowfall upon skin.
And in the next breath, all remaining Inevitabilities and golems screeched as one.
Their bodies imploded in sheer existential terror.

Their monstrous limbs convulsed. Their many eyes cracked like glass beneath a hammer. Their jagged, writhing masses burst, turning into dazzling white stars that floated through the cold air like offerings... all of them moving toward the figure that had commanded them.
Toward Sigrid.
She didn’t reach out.
She simply received.
And in front of Noah, a prompt unfolded like a blooming petal, elegant and heavy with implication.

|You have witnessed the first action of The Budding Young Living Order. As the one who has bound the Living Order, once her authority reaches sufficient maturity, you shall gain access to Living Order Authority. Living Orders may also be born in the Early Veiled Shore and Festivals of Existence at that time.|
His lips parted slightly, a breath escaping into the icy domain as his eyes gleamed with unspoken anticipation. Glorious anticipation!
Access to Living Order.
To that Authority.
The domain before them began to shimmer as over a hundred radiant Treasure Chests bloomed in neat clusters across the white sea where Inevitabilities once screeched.
Loot.
Magisterial chests of Loot!
All around, voices rose in wonder and hushed shock.
Even Master Neinoro couldn’t help himself.
"That..." His voice broke the silence like a polite blade. "That Authority... it bears resemblance to the power the Foldless Ones wield. How fortunate we are to witness such magnificence!"
He was smiling brightly.
Noah’s gaze slid toward him with disdain.
Master Neinoro bowed low, arms out, robes pristine and posture perfect as he looked towards Sigrid.
"For your intervention, we are thankful," he said, voice full of performative warmth. "Truly, all those present benefit from your blessed act."
Sigrid didn’t blink. She looked at him like one would look at a particularly annoying draft of wind. "I didn’t do it for you," she replied flatly.
Master Neinoro straightened with a soft chuckle, brushing her words away as though they were mere dust from his shoulder.
"Of course not," he said with a gallant grin. "But gratitude must be expressed nonetheless. After all, the Fold Dwellers of these blessed Folds will partake in the blessings you left behind."
He moved casually before anyone could object.
Gliding across the air with practiced grace, he reached one of the nearest Treasure Chests.

His fingers extended- calmly, politely- and as the golden chest opened, bundles of radiant loot danced out. Glimmering fragments of authority, vibrant cores of frozen complexity, even crystalline veins of dormant Inevitability remnants containing a sense of...Everything.
Noah watched.
His smile, faint and cold, did not reach his eyes.
Sigrid’s brow furrowed as she said slowly, "What do you think you’re doing?"
He turned to her, blinking with innocent confusion as if her question surprised him.
"We are all cultivators along the same path," he said smoothly. "The journey toward advancement is not one of isolation. Resources, like trials, are meant to be shared."
She didn’t respond.
He continued.

"You are clearly... immensely powerful already." A feigned humility laced his tone. "So surely you do not require every chest here? As you’ve said, you acted not for us, but out of necessity. But now, the trial is complete. Its rewards, by the spirit of fairness and the principles of cultivation, belong to all of us equally."
He gestured widely to the other Masters of Existence and Primarchs still watching from the sidelines, then smiled toward Sigrid as though he were the embodiment of compassion itself.
"Surely the Foldless Ones observing these trials would agree. They designed these mechanics, did they not? And no design favors the greedy."
Noah’s smile remained.
So did his silence.
But in his chest...he felt something vibrant begin to simmer.
It was...amusement.
Because it was always the same.
From Primarchs to Masters of Existence to Originus Venerants...when they saw brilliance, they only ever thought of how to steal from it.
And Master Neinoro, wrapped in civility, soaked in self-righteousness, was no different.
He simply smiled more while doing it.
And so Noah smiled too.
Quietly.
As if he’d just realized how enjoyable the next few minutes would be!

chapters.title: Chapter 3892: Sin of Association! I
paragraphs: CLAP! CLAP! CLAP!

Noah’s hands came together slowly, the sound of his clap cracking across the frozen sea like distant thunder. The weight of his presence stretched outward, brushing against the chests of every Master of Existence and Primarch here. His voice followed, calm and stripped of all pretense.
"Very good," he said as he glanced at the glowing treasures surrounding them. "Now then... is there anyone else who believes they have a rightful stake in the Treasure Chests here?"
The stillness that followed wasn’t silence. It was caution. It was reverence. The kind of hush that came before waves of existence collapsed!
HUUM!
Power emanated from him, cold and absolute. The kind of authority that didn’t beg for compliance, but it expected it!
Noah did not raise his voice. He didn’t need to. The reverberation of his authority, paired with the Glyph that pulsed like a slow heartbeat on his forehead, was enough to still the weavings of many.
And yet.
Master Neinoro scoffed.

Standing proudly, he turned, his white robes pristine and the glow of a calculated righteousness lighting his pale eyes. He gazed out over the gathered entities with the weight of false kinship, his voice ringing as though he were the herald of justice.

"Fellow Masters of Existence," he called. "We all know the principles of fairness and cultivation. Even the Foldless Ones would stand on our side. One Master of Existence cannot dictate the fate of us all, nor hoard rewards meant for all those who participated. If we stand together-"
Noah’s voice sliced through him like a blade honed on the edge of infinity.
"For an insignificant extra," Noah said, "you have already taken up far too much time."
A hush deeper than frost followed.
Master Neinoro stiffened, the authority behind those words grazing his existence like a cold blade. And then, Noah spoke again.
"You seem desperate to die today," he said. "So I’ll grant you that death."
The Glyph of the Protagonist flashed with golden brilliance, and Noah’s aura erupted in a lancing burst. Power flooded toward Master Neinoro like judgment descending from above!
And yet... Master Neinoro did not flinch.
He didn’t even move.
Instead, a brilliant white-gold shield bloomed around him glpriously!.
Intricate, ancient, and unshatterable- formed of something unmistakable.
Living Origin Authority!
There was a collective inhale across the frozen sea as dozens of eyes widened in disbelief. Even Sigrid’s pupils constricted with sudden gravity, her body tilting ever so slightly toward Noah.
Master Neinoro...had protection.
Master Neinoro bowed toward the glowing barrier now enveloping him, his eyes never leaving Noah’s.
"I express my thanks," he said with an infuriating smile towards the authority protecting him. "To the great Foldless One for preserving peace and ensuring justice."
He said the words like a man who knew exactly when to cry for mercy and when to spit in your face.
The silence afterward was suffocating.
Until a voice that should not have been heard reverberated through the entire region- cold and unfathomably ancient, filled with layers of untouchable judgment.
|Fold Dwellers stemming from Folds under the shade of Living Paradoxes may kill each other... but they may not raise their hands to those from Folds under the shade of other Living Existences.|
BOOM!
The words fell like a mountain, the very frost cracking beneath its weight. All across the glacial expanse, figures bowed their heads instinctively when they heard the voice.
Kalysta’s golden hair swayed forward in submission of shock. Master Etheopa’s face turned ashen as her form sank in reverence!
Because all knew what this was.
A Foldless One.
An Entity above the conflict of Fold Dwellers!
A being whose presence could silence entire folds.
The domain stilled under the weight of its voice, as if the very Yggdrasil trees feared to creak in protest.
To be a Foldless One was to carry the birthright of existence itself. They stood outside the typical hierarchy. They were hierarchy!
And even if they weren’t physically present, their words shifted edicts and forced judgment to move in unnatural rhythms.
Noah stood still, recognizing the voice of the Living Origin, Altheon!
His posture remained unyielding, though his eyes narrowed as he watched Neinoro still bowing, head lowered, but eyes lifted.
Mocking.
He had known. All along, he had known that this protection would come.
And still, Noah’s voice echoed with the steel of defiance.
"Why?" he asked. "Why is it that such protection is granted only to Fold Dwellers from the Folds under Living Existences? What crime have those from Paradoxical Folds committed?"
That question.
It shattered the silence more than any scream could have.
Dozens of eyes widened.
To speak against a Foldless One...
To question one...it was truly Madness.
Madness!
Insanity.
A death sentence.
Many Masters of Existence tensed, expecting his form to be obliterated in a moment of judgment. Some even looked away, unwilling to watch the splintering of a rising star.
But the voice that answered came cold, resolute, and impassive.
|Fold Dwellers from Paradoxical Folds have done nothing wrong. They bear no crime... save the sin of association.|
Noah’s fingers curled slightly, his jaw tightening.

|But when it comes to Paradoxes, even that is enough. Enough to strip them of certain protections. Enough to ensure that while this Labyrinth may allow them passage to the Transcendent Folds to be trained on how to fight against True Inevitabilities... they will still be watched. They will be tested. They will be reminded.|
HUUM!
The frost on the ground deepened.
The cold wasn’t from temperature anymore.
It permeated from the uttered words!
The crime of association.
The inheritance of sin.
Noah’s heart remained calm.
Cold.
Sharper than before.
He didn’t need to speak again.
Because now, they all knew who he was.
They had seen him burn Hannibal to nothing. They had watched Torus beg before disappearing into ash.
They all knew that he and those he killed...came under a light of Folds that were under the influence of Living Paradoxes!
And now they saw him defy the decree of a Foldless One and still stand unbroken!

chapters.title: Chapter 3893: Sin of Association! II
paragraphs: At the words of the Foldless One, Altheon, Master Neinoro rose tall as if vindicated by the very air, brushing imaginary dust from his white robes as the glow of the Living Origin Authority curled protectively around him. His tone rang with clean-cut indignation, each syllable sharpened like a knife.
"It makes sense now!" he declared. "One Master of Existence distastefully devouring others, and another murdering him in turn. It all stinks of contradiction... of chaos... of Paradox!"
HUUM!
Paradox!
It was always paradox that was problematic. Since the Earliest Folds!
He turned toward Noah as if pronouncing a sentence. "The bane of all existence."
The words slithered like venom through the gathering.

He swept his arms outward, not toward Noah, but to all the Masters and Primarchs floating on frost-covered branches and Yggdrasil roots. His voice rose, carried on falsified concern and hollow leadership.

"Fellow Masters of Existence," he said with performative solemnity, "surely the resources here would be best reserved for those of stable folds. Not for those whose very nature undermines the balance of Existence. The strength of those here, combined, would elevate all."
His eyes glanced toward Kalysta, Master Etheopa... and finally, Noah.
He was standing taller now. Emboldened.
Because he wasn’t afraid.
He wasn’t alone.
This wasn’t the first time Master Neinoro had felt the favor of Foldless Ones.
No, his steps here had already been mapped by whispered promises of a Living Law long before he set foot in this Labyrinth. Promises of transformation. Of freedom from the identity of a Fold Dweller.
Of becoming... a Living Existence should he succesfully clear the Living Origin Labyrinth.
That was the true source of his confidence. Not his strength. Not his insight. But the path he believed he had been given.

He had been told that if he could clear the Living Origin Labyrinth, he would be one of the chosen to pass into the Transcendent Folds beyond. Into the chaotic, death-strewn realm near the Loom itself- where Inevitabilities reigned and where, if one survived, even a Fold Dweller could ascend to something greater.
That was his wager.
That was the reason he could taunt a being like Noah and still smile.
Because he had backing.
And Noah, in his mind, did not.
So when other Masters began to drift subtly toward the treasure chests, emboldened by Neinoro’s claims, Noah’s gaze grew colder!
"You think," he said softly, "just because someone big told you they’ll protect you... that you can do whatever stupid shit you want?"
He looked at the man with a calm, measured stare, as if studying the Existence beneath the skin.
"Okay."
Raw Power versus True Power!
Always, there could be discrepancy when one did not accurate gauge their True Power.
And discrepancies often led to disappointment!
He turned toward Sigrid.
She didn’t need any words. Her golden eyes lifted to the crimson-gold haze above, toward the sphere that floated like an unseen eye. The gaze of Altheon.
Her voice didn’t waver. It carried like a tide of Order.
"All treasures made available by my actions are to go straight to him. No one else from any Folds."
The word him rang heavier than gold. The wind itself seemed to falter, waiting.
Master Neinoro’s brow twitched. He straightened his robe, but his hands curled tightly behind his back as he nearly harrumphed.

Her words felt like command. No, they were command. And within seconds, as if Time itself had to answer her decree, the voice of Altheon returned almost as if it were disliking the words about to be uttered!
|All resources in this Final Labyrinth Domain are for... him.|
BOOM!
The pronoun landed like a meteor.
Not Paradox. Not Fold Dweller.
Him.
And they all knew who that meant.
Even those who didn’t dare say it.
The gathered Masters and Primarchs turned slowly towards Noah, others towards Sigrid. Some with awe. Some with dawning horror. Others with envy.
Who was she... that she could shift the will of a Foldless One?
And who was he... that she called down such favor for him alone?
Noah didn’t blink.

He simply raised his hand, and from his fingertips, golden strings of authority unfurled like silk, weaving through the air like hungry roots. They found every treasure chest scattered across the vast branches and frozen wind, threading around them in elegant lines of ownership.
And one by one... they disappeared.
The chests folded out of space, drawn toward the one who had been named.
The one who stood beside Order.

Noah’s gaze turned again toward Master Neinoro, whose smile had begun to fracture. His face still wore a look of civility, but there was a stutter in his aura. A twitch of calculation trying to rewrite itself.
"The command," Noah said, "was for all resources to come to me, you sad excuse of an existence."
His voice struck like thunder. "Give back what you took."
Master Neinoro lifted his head slowly, casting his gaze to the air above as if still expecting Altheon’s voice to intervene again. But there was nothing.
Only silence.
Only the cold.
And Sigrid, standing beside Noah, radiant with calm certainty.
Master Neinoro’s mouth twitched.
Then, slowly, reluctantly, he waved his hand.
An orb of golden light floated forward. It hovered toward Noah’s palm like a sheep returning to the shepherd.
The moment it touched his hand, light bloomed as it also disappeared!
And the moment it did, there was a subtle change.
Altheon’s voice once again echoed across the realm, cold as the deepest void.

|All trials and resources in the Final Domain of the Living Origin Labyrinth have been claimed. Those who have made it and will make it into this region will now gain passage into the Transcendent Origin Battlefront Folds.|
HUUM!
Transcendent Origin Battlefront Folds!
A stillness followed the words.
Because those who knew what that meant... truly knew what it meant.
The Transcendent Battlefronts were a prize...and a place of horror.
They were a warzone.
A contested edge of Existence where Foldless Ones had pushed forward toward the Loom itself, where Inevitabilities were real, and not imitations.
Where the chance to ascend existed... only through slaughter.
The frost beneath their feet cracked.
The Yggdrasil branches groaned in the distant skies.
And in the silence, Noah stood at the center of it all.
Unyielding. Quintessential, and with eyes unfathomably bright as while all of this occured...the slow construction of a wonder of a Tower inside his Existence neared completion!

sentences.text: At the words of the Foldless One, Altheon, Master Neinoro rose tall as if vindicated by the very air, brushing imaginary dust from his white robes as the glow of the Living Origin Authority curled protectively around him.
His tone rang with clean-cut indignation, each syllable sharpened like a knife.
"It makes sense now!" he declared.
"One Master of Existence distastefully devouring others, and another murdering him in turn.
It all stinks of contradiction... of chaos... of Paradox!"
HUUM!
Paradox!
It was always paradox that was problematic.
Since the Earliest Folds!
He turned toward Noah as if pronouncing a sentence.
"The bane of all existence."
The words slithered like venom through the gathering.
He swept his arms outward, not toward Noah, but to all the Masters and Primarchs floating on frost-covered branches and Yggdrasil roots.
His voice rose, carried on falsified concern and hollow leadership.
"Fellow Masters of Existence," he said with performative solemnity, "surely the resources here would be best reserved for those of stable folds.
Not for those whose very nature undermines the balance of Existence.
The strength of those here, combined, would elevate all."
His eyes glanced toward Kalysta, Master Etheopa... and finally, Noah.
He was standing taller now.
Emboldened.
Because he wasn’t afraid.
He wasn’t alone.
This wasn’t the first time Master Neinoro had felt the favor of Foldless Ones.
No, his steps here had already been mapped by whispered promises of a Living Law long before he set foot in this Labyrinth.
Promises of transformation.
Of freedom from the identity of a Fold Dweller.
Of becoming... a Living Existence should he succesfully clear the Living Origin Labyrinth.
That was the true source of his confidence.
Not his strength.
Not his insight.
But the path he believed he had been given.
He had been told that if he could clear the Living Origin Labyrinth, he would be one of the chosen to pass into the Transcendent Folds beyond.
Into the chaotic, death-strewn realm near the Loom itself- where Inevitabilities reigned and where, if one survived, even a Fold Dweller could ascend to something greater.
That was his wager.
That was the reason he could taunt a being like Noah and still smile.
Because he had backing.
And Noah, in his mind, did not.
So when other Masters began to drift subtly toward the treasure chests, emboldened by Neinoro’s claims, Noah’s gaze grew colder!
"You think," he said softly, "just because someone big told you they’ll protect you... that you can do whatever stupid shit you want?"
He looked at the man with a calm, measured stare, as if studying the Existence beneath the skin.
"Okay."
Raw Power versus True Power!
Always, there could be discrepancy when one did not accurate gauge their True Power.
And discrepancies often led to disappointment!
He turned toward Sigrid.
She didn’t need any words.
Her golden eyes lifted to the crimson-gold haze above, toward the sphere that floated like an unseen eye.
The gaze of Altheon.
Her voice didn’t waver.
It carried like a tide of Order.

No one else from any Folds."
The word him rang heavier than gold.
The wind itself seemed to falter, waiting.
Master Neinoro’s brow twitched.

Her words felt like command.
No, they were command.

Not Fold Dweller.
Him.
And they all knew who that meant.
Even those who didn’t dare say it.

Some with dawning horror.
Others with envy.

And who was he... that she called down such favor for him alone?
Noah didn’t blink.
He simply raised his hand, and from his fingertips, golden strings of authority unfurled like silk, weaving through the air like hungry roots.

And one by one... they disappeared.
The chests folded out of space, drawn toward the one who had been named.
The one who stood beside Order.

His face still wore a look of civility, but there was a stutter in his aura.
A twitch of calculation trying to rewrite itself.

chapters.title: Chapter 3894: Sin of Association! III
paragraphs: The cold branches of Yggdrasil pulsed lightly above the glacial winds, and beneath their shimmering white canopy, silence descended in ripples.
The air no longer trembled with chaos or battle.
It hung suspended by something far more absolute!
The domain that had moments ago crackled with the tension of potential violence, with the quiet hope of transcendence and ascension, now pulsed with anticipation. Dread. And awe.
The figures of Masters of Existence and Primarchs, scattered across the white expanse, stood tall and triumphant. Some had fists clenched in quiet victory, others looked skyward!
They had heard the words of a Foldless One.
They had been granted passage to the Transcendent Origin Battlefront Folds!
To them, this meant only one thing- hope for advancement. The hope of finally breaking through.
The hope of continuing to build the elusive Tower of Origin in a realm where even the smallest step forward was paved with suffering and the waves of failures.

Devouring another Master of Existence was the easiest route. Hannibal had taken it, brazen and brutal. But that too had ended. Few could tread that path openly and survive the consequence in many Folds that had Living Existences seeking to impose order.
It made it truly difficult to raise one’s power if they could not devour others!
The rest clung to whispers of panaceas. To glimmers of Existential treasures. To slivers of Inevitabilities.
They had seen the proof in this Labyrinth.
Even the Imitation Mutated Inevitabilities had yielded treasures that allowed for a rapid rise in power.
The real ones stemming from actual Inevitabilities in the Battlefront...would offer more!
They hungered.
And as they had such complex emotions...
HUUM!
Without sound, without flash or warning, a golden wave struck out instsntly across this domain.
WAP.
It was soft, almost elegant in its delivery. But its effect was undeniable.
All those expressions- the elation, the anticipation- froze.
Literally.
Every figure, every swirling authority, stopped.
Master Neinoro. Master Etheopa. Kalysta. All Fold Dwellers here!
Weavings of Existence that had once pulsed with boundless pride dimmed like dying stars. Faces blank. Bodies rigid.
Frozen in the golden wave’s grip.
Noah’s head tilted slightly.
His eyes sharpened as he recognized the authority of the Living Origin, Altheon, who had just spoken grandly!
The same fucker that tried to kill his body of Ozymandias- how could he forget his signature aura?
Sigrid stood beside him, unflinching and untouched.
They alone remained aware, unfrozen.
Noah’s weavings pulsed gently in his body, intricate layers of Authority adapting instantly, dancing with unseen threads. Not even his eyelids flinched.
But deep inside, he analyzed.

Altheon’s authority had swept across this domain in a whisper and paralyzed all within it without even alerting their senses. It was an authority dense enough to suppress Masters of Existence and Primarchs alike in a moment of stillness they didn’t even know had occurred.
Fascinating.
The Glyph of the Protagonist at his forehead spun slowly as it registered the scale and rhythm of the action. Hundreds of thousands of lattices aligned silently in his mind.
A moment later, the figure began to descend- layered in blinding white and gold, ancient and impossible- he needed no introduction.
Altheon.
He looked stern as he voiced out.

"I have followed the commands of the Young Miss," Altheon said as his luminous body took full form- his halos and wings flashing gloriously, "and permitted her to complete the Living Origin Labyrinth in its entirety."
His gaze swept the realm.
And then paused.
Upon Noah.
The look was not violent. Nor respectful.
It was displeased.
Altheon’s eyes narrowed, his tone flattening.
"I would have frozen you as well... but the attachment the Young Miss bears for you is clear. It is the sole reason you remain standing."
Noah smiled.
Openly.
Calmly.

He simply looked back- his mind already measuring the authority used to paralyze the others, calculating what level of resistance it would take to undo it... and how long before he could wield such power himself.
Beside him, Sigrid was still as a blade. Her golden-white eyes shimmered with frost as she looked upon Altheon with no deference, only thoughtfulness.
Then, she spoke.
Her voice was not emotional. It was steady. Resolute.
"I will not return to the folds of the Honored Living Origins."
BOOM!
Altheon’s expression cracked.
Not in anger.
In a sense of frustration and grief.

His glow rippled, wavering as he lowered his gaze briefly. "Young Miss... I am bound to serve and protect you because of your status as I will listen to you. But I am also a Living Origin. There are oaths I-"
"Listen first," Sigrid interrupted, lifting her hand.
It was not a request. It was an Order!
Even Noah looked at her closely now, his gaze slightly narrowed as he saw Sigrid speak authoritatively towards a Living Origin- as if she was more...confident and sure of herself.
Of her identity.
Sigrid continued, her voice cold and sharp. "Among the Living Origins, only a few Prime Living Origins like you... and a handful of Honored Origins... know of my existence."

She stepped forward, chin high, every line of her posture screaming Order. "My disappearance was a blessing. No one knows I’m alive. Which makes me safe. Letting my identity be known again puts me in danger as I am sure you understand what the resurgence of a Living Order represents. The Living Order. What would Living Paradoxes do if they knew? Other Living Existences?"
HUUM!
Her words settled like a cold mist. Altheon’s glow dimmed.
And then, the true edge of her voice came forth, low and full of dreadful knowledge.
"Can you say with certainty... that all Living Origins are aligned? That none have allied themselves to other Living Existences? That none are bound to the Living Paradoxes?"
Altheon’s golden frame pulsed with power!
"No," he said quietly. "That is...not possible. I do not believe—"
"You don’t believe," she cut in again, "but you also don’t know. You can’t know."

Her eyes gleamed with a glow both terrible and majestic. "I am becoming the Living Order. The Living Order. I can feel things now that I couldn’t before. Paradox has not faded. It festers pervasively now as it did in the Earliest Folds. Just like before, Paradox is widespread...and Inevitable!"
WAA!
She said such words as at this, Noah couldn’t help but smile and speak out.

"When it comes to Living Paradoxes mixing with Living Origins, I know a bit about this..." he said, voice lazy and light. "There’s a Young Paradox stemming in the Paradoxical Folds...said to be the offspring of a Living Origin and a Living Paradox."
Altheon’s body pulsed in a terrifying manner at these words as if they could not be true!
The air around him pulsed. His hands buzzed as his voice turned into a sharp whisper!
"Who? Who is that?!"
Altheon had his weavings swirl as he thought of the Young Paradox he nearly killed.
Ozymandias!
If they are born of both Paradox and Origin... then that would explain a little of their mutation on why they do not produce Inevitabilities!
Even Sigrid’s eyes flickered with interest as Noah shrugged faintly. "I don’t know much. No Fold Dwellers do. Just that the Young Paradox has two names. One’s Ozymandias."
BOOM!
Altheon’s body stiffened.
Noah looked him dead in the eye.
"The other," he said, voice calm as still water, "is Aetheron."

chapters.title: Chapter 3895: Sin of Association! IV
paragraphs: Altheon’s radiant body trembled faintly.
The names rippled across his thoughts like thunderclaps cast in golden glass.
"Ozymandias..." he uttered first, the syllables curling with memory.
Then, slower and sharper....
"Aetheron."
A name he had not known.
His mind buzzed as he began connecting threads of knowledge- well, knowledge based on what little information he was given!
Thauron... did that bastard not tell him everything?!
His glow dimmed with thought as he looked once again toward the boy- the man before him. Noah. Cold eyes. Tyrannically calm before a Foldless One even though he was a mere Fold Dweller.
He could somewhat see why this being had attracted the attention of the Young Miss.

And just now, he revealed more information about the Paradox that did not produce Inevitabilities as through this, Altheon could share with the others that they were looking for an abomination...born from Paradox and Origin!
Since Living Paradoxes now surrounded that being, he would have to ask for one of their operatives planted among the Living Paradoxes to gather information around the names...Ozymandias and Aetheron!
They were one and the same, and the abomination that did not produce Inevitabilities which had to die!
He spoke out in his grand voice.
"You have contributed knowledge far more than you realize," Altheon said slowly. "Because of this, I will ease up on you. I will look past your sin of association- for now."
Noah’s expression didn’t change, but he smiled while hiding his silent laughter!
Should he, an Early Creature, feel so honored that a mere Living Origin marked for Death would now look slightly more favorable to him?
His gaze flicked to Sigrid as if granting her the floor, not even bothering to reply as he simply name dropped Aetheron to muddy the waters of Ozymandias.
Sigrid stepped forward without hesitation as her voice came smooth, curved with control.

"Regardless," she said, "we both know trust is a luxury we can’t afford. Not entirely. If I return to the Living Origins now, disclosed and known, I risk assassination before I even have the chance to become what I am meant to be."
Her chin lifted ever so slightly.
"Would you like that on your existence? As your responsibility?"
Altheon said nothing.
His frame stood glorious in glacial air, the winds curling around him, golden white robes and all as his ancient mind weighed her words.
Eventually, he broke the silence, slow and grim.
"Young Miss... just tell me what you are proposing."
Sigrid’s answer was immediate as if she had already thought about many things.
"You may alert Royal Origin Calypso," she said, "and Duke Gwendolyn."
She turned her head slightly, her voice low and sharp. "I do not sense the corruption of Order in either of them with certainty."
The glacial branches above groaned again, crystalline leaves shivering under her quiet command.
"Let them know I still live."
Her tone darkened now.
"I will forge myself into the Living Order with my own hands, Complexity by complexity, Purity by purity. And that can only happen... if I walk through the chaos of existence."
HUUM!
Noah watched her with narrowed eyes. He could feel the pulse of her ambition, the glory of her reason, and the depth of her resolve!
"I will enter the Transcendent Origin Battlefront Folds," she said. "Accompanied by him."
She nodded toward Noah without a glance.
"And for safety, you may trail us from a distance and observe. Or Duke Gwendolyn can send those she trusts to keep watch. That is my will. And you...will follow it."
Her words fell like stones from a throne, each syllable deliberate.
There was no room for interpretation. No room for negotiation.
Altheon’s glow dimmed again.

Silent, he turned his gaze between Sigrid and Noah, his ancient mind slicing through possibilities, calculating thousands of probabilities and weavings of potential timelines of how things would unfold in a breath.
Finally, he inclined his head.
"I will escort and protect Young Miss in the Battlefront Folds," he said solemnly. "And I will notify Royal Origin Calypso and Duke Gwendolyn."
A brief pause.
"Mmm," Sigrid nodded, pleased.
Then her eyes sharpened.
"I shouldn’t need to say this," she continued, "but do not mention more than you must. My new face. My company. If you speak out of turn..."
Her voice quieted to a whisper.
"You will earn the wrath of the future Living Order. Do you want that?"
The majestic being pulsed with power.
His gilded face remained staunch as he lowered his head.
"No, Young Miss."
The air grew colder. Thicker.
"Come here," she said.
Noah’s eyes blinked once.
The words weren’t loud, but they moved like a command born at the beginning of time.
Altheon, the Foldless One, floated forward at such a command.
He moved slowly, solemnly, the air bending around him as if even space bowed to his step. He stopped before Sigrid, his head lowered.
Sigrid extended her hand, pale and slender.
With no hesitation, Altheon bent forward and pressed his lips to the back of it.
It was not romantic.
It was reverence.
She held his gaze as he rose.
"You will not disrespect those around me," she said.
Her voice turned deadly and perfect.
"You know who I mean."
She stepped closer.
"And if you follow me... if you serve properly... then I will elevate you."
Her breath was steady.
"I will give you position, standing, name. Easily a Royal Living Origin. Or even for you to replace one of the 81 Dukes of the Transcendent Origin Folds."
Her gaze held him in place.
"If you care nothing for titles, then you will hold something greater, the personal favor of I, the only Living Order."
Altheon met her eyes. He turned to Noah. And then back again.
The pride in him still whispered resistance. But the calculations, always the calculations, outweighed it!
He lowered his head.
"Understood, Young Miss."
His voice grew quieter.

"He will receive no disrespect from me. But... by the sin of association, he- and the others from the Paradoxical Folds will still be looked down upon by other Fold Dwellers and the Living Existences in the Battlefront Folds."
The cold winds stirred softly in response.
Noah said nothing.
He simply smiled.
Altheon’s form hovered still in the air as he added, the words ringing with cold finality.
"All Fold Dwellers will be claimed and sponsored by the Living Existences under whose Folds they were born," he said. "You... will be claimed by none. No sponsor. No protector."
Noah did not flinch. His smile curled with mockery at such words.
When was he not an outcast?!

They were one and the same, and the abomination that did not produce Inevitabilities which had to die!
He spoke out in his grand voice.
"You have contributed knowledge far more than you realize," Altheon said slowly.
"Because of this, I will ease up on you.
I will look past your sin of association- for now."
Noah’s expression didn’t change, but he smiled while hiding his silent laughter!
Should he, an Early Creature, feel so honored that a mere Living Origin marked for Death would now look slightly more favorable to him?
His gaze flicked to Sigrid as if granting her the floor, not even bothering to reply as he simply name dropped Aetheron to muddy the waters of Ozymandias.
Sigrid stepped forward without hesitation as her voice came smooth, curved with control.
"Regardless," she said, "we both know trust is a luxury we can’t afford.
Not entirely.
If I return to the Living Origins now, disclosed and known, I risk assassination before I even have the chance to become what I am meant to be."
Her chin lifted ever so slightly.
"Would you like that on your existence?
As your responsibility?"
Altheon said nothing.
His frame stood glorious in glacial air, the winds curling around him, golden white robes and all as his ancient mind weighed her words.
Eventually, he broke the silence, slow and grim.
"Young Miss... just tell me what you are proposing."
Sigrid’s answer was immediate as if she had already thought about many things.
"You may alert Royal Origin Calypso," she said, "and Duke Gwendolyn."
She turned her head slightly, her voice low and sharp.
"I do not sense the corruption of Order in either of them with certainty."
The glacial branches above groaned again, crystalline leaves shivering under her quiet command.
"Let them know I still live."
Her tone darkened now.
"I will forge myself into the Living Order with my own hands, Complexity by complexity, Purity by purity.
And that can only happen... if I walk through the chaos of existence."
HUUM!
Noah watched her with narrowed eyes.
He could feel the pulse of her ambition, the glory of her reason, and the depth of her resolve!
"I will enter the Transcendent Origin Battlefront Folds," she said.
"Accompanied by him."
She nodded toward Noah without a glance.
"And for safety, you may trail us from a distance and observe.
Or Duke Gwendolyn can send those she trusts to keep watch.
That is my will.
And you...will follow it."
Her words fell like stones from a throne, each syllable deliberate.
There was no room for interpretation.
No room for negotiation.
Altheon’s glow dimmed again.

Silent, he turned his gaze between Sigrid and Noah, his ancient mind slicing through possibilities, calculating thousands of probabilities and weavings of potential timelines of how things would unfold in a breath.
Finally, he inclined his head.
"I will escort and protect Young Miss in the Battlefront Folds," he said solemnly.
"And I will notify Royal Origin Calypso and Duke Gwendolyn."
A brief pause.
"Mmm," Sigrid nodded, pleased.
Then her eyes sharpened.
"I shouldn’t need to say this," she continued, "but do not mention more than you must.
My new face.
My company.
If you speak out of turn..."
Her voice quieted to a whisper.
"You will earn the wrath of the future Living Order.
Do you want that?"
The majestic being pulsed with power.
His gilded face remained staunch as he lowered his head.
"No, Young Miss."
The air grew colder.
Thicker.
"Come here," she said.
Noah’s eyes blinked once.
The words weren’t loud, but they moved like a command born at the beginning of time.
Altheon, the Foldless One, floated forward at such a command.
He moved slowly, solemnly, the air bending around him as if even space bowed to his step.
He stopped before Sigrid, his head lowered.
Sigrid extended her hand, pale and slender.
With no hesitation, Altheon bent forward and pressed his lips to the back of it.
It was not romantic.
It was reverence.
She held his gaze as he rose.
"You will not disrespect those around me," she said.
Her voice turned deadly and perfect.
"You know who I mean."
She stepped closer.
"And if you follow me... if you serve properly... then I will elevate you."
Her breath was steady.
"I will give you position, standing, name.
Easily a Royal Living Origin.
Or even for you to replace one of the 81 Dukes of the Transcendent Origin Folds."
Her gaze held him in place.
"If you care nothing for titles, then you will hold something greater, the personal favor of I, the only Living Order."
Altheon met her eyes.
He turned to Noah.
And then back again.
The pride in him still whispered resistance.
But the calculations, always the calculations, outweighed it!
He lowered his head.
"Understood, Young Miss."
His voice grew quieter.
"He will receive no disrespect from me.
But... by the sin of association, he- and the others from the Paradoxical Folds will still be looked down upon by other Fold Dwellers and the Living Existences in the Battlefront Folds."
The cold winds stirred softly in response.
Noah said nothing.
He simply smiled.
Altheon’s form hovered still in the air as he added, the words ringing with cold finality.
"All Fold Dwellers will be claimed and sponsored by the Living Existences under whose Folds they were born," he said.
"You... will be claimed by none.
No sponsor.
No protector."
Noah did not flinch.
His smile curled with mockery at such words.
When was he not an outcast?!

chapters.title: Chapter 3896: Foundation I
paragraphs: The role of the one looked down on was not new to Noah!
Beside him, Sigrid merely tilted her head. The ringlets of her pale dark and white hair caught the light, gleaming like a halo of frost.
"You don’t need to worry about that," she said. "As long as you play your part. And is a Sponsor really needed if you and other Living Origins will constantly be watching my back?"
Altheon did not argue.
"I understand, Young Miss," he said, bowing his head slightly. "I will get started."
His luminous figure shimmered and faded.
The golden haze blanketing the frozen domain dissipated slowly.
And all around them, time returned to its flow.
The Masters of Existence and Primarchs stirred once more.
None of them knew. None of them even noticed. Their expressions remained unchanged, their thoughts continuing along paths interrupted only by the barest blink. As if no pause had ever occurred.
They resumed looking around, eyes filled with anticipation and awe.

Noah’s gaze swept over them. These beings, powerful as they were, hadn’t even realized their existences had been paused. That their threads had been severed for a single beat of judgment. He shook his head slowly.
"They don’t even know," he muttered.
His thoughts turned. If Altheon had tried to freeze him...
Would he have succeeded?
The Glyph of the Protagonist spun in quiet brilliance against his forehead. It glowed with pride, with defiance. And deep within his being, something ancient pulsed. Something that did not yield.
An Early Creature could not and should not be frozen by one less!
Not completely!
As he thought this, in the next instant...
BOOM!
The skies shattered like brittle crystal above them.

The frozen clouds of radiant frost cracked apart as the heavens split, and from the void, a towering doorway unfolded. White-gold and endless, etched with runes of Living Origin so intricate they seemed to whisper to the soul.
The Gateway to the Transcendent Origin Battlefront Folds had appeared.
Altheon’s voice thundered once more, this time cold and clear, stripped of all earlier warmth.
|The Gate is open. Victors of the Labyrinth- pass through, and you shall arrive in the Transcendent Origin Battlefront Folds.|
HUUM!
All around, Masters of Existence and Primarchs turned to one another. Their bodies blurred into streams of celestial light, surging toward the shattered glimmering skies!
Excitement. Purpose. The promise of battle and treasure- of progression!
Among them, Master Neinoro turned back, casting his long calculating gaze at Sigrid and Noah.
He bowed low toward Sigrid, the curve of his spine as smooth as oil.
"I hope none of my earlier actions caused offense, Honored Miss," he said, tone silken and insincere. "In the Folds ahead, if you require help... I will ensure all of us are ready to assist."
Then he turned his face toward Noah and nodded, his smile slick.
He turned and ascended, a stream of white light vanishing into the gateway as others from the Law Folds followed in his wake.
Noah watched him go without blinking.
His eyes then slid to Kalysta and Master Etheopa.
They stood silently beneath the branches of frost-laden trees, gazes lifted toward the open gateway above. Wonder and hesitation shone in their eyes.
He floated toward them, a bit of pity flashing in his eyes as he spoke to them.
"If you go through," he said, voice calm and cold, "expect no kindness. You are from Folds overseeing by Living Paradoxes. That alone will make you targets."
Kalysta’s expression darkened, but she nodded.
Master Etheopa stepped forward, her face grave.
"We will wait," she said. "Until Master Shen and the rest of of those from the Veiled Sunfolds reach this domain. We’ll go with numbers... not alone."
Noah nodded once.
Then he turned, ignoring the glimmering brightness in Kalysta’s gaze as it trailed after him.
He returned to Sigrid and stopped at her side.
"Let’s go," he said. "To the Battlefront."
"Mmm..." Sigrid spared one last glance and a nod to Kalysta and those of the Veiled Sunfolds before she went ahead.
Together, they ascended. Two figures- one crowned in tyranny, the other in fate- rising toward the threshold of the Transcendent Origin Battlefront Folds.
And while such a thing happened, Noah smiled as he sensed something lock into place.
Something bloomed inside of him- deep, vast, monumental!
And with it came a prompt. Clear. Absolute.

|The Early Sacred Living Infinity Tower of Osmont centered around your Blood of an Early Creature has been arduously and gloriously forged through the complex fuel of the Early Living Marine Lifeforms stemming from the Early Veiled Shore.|
|Your Complexity Quotient and Purity Quotient have both been increased by +500,000 from the completion of this single Tower of Osmont.|
|Since a Tower of Osmont is completed, the Heart of an Early Creature can now begin to be formed. The resources required for its completion are unknown, but expected to be exceedingly high.|
Noah remained composed- eyes narrowing, mind threading through implications with practiced ease. Yet within, a deeper tide stirred. One he did not voice. One he rarely acknowledged aloud.
Satisfaction.
And hunger. Hunger to exceed and overcome himself even more!
A breath later, he turned his thoughts inward.
In the Early Veiled Shore.
Warm mist clung to the vibrant cerulean sands, curling around pale spiraling shells that shimmered with embedded runes older than most Folds had ever recorded.

Waves kissed the shoreline in patient cadence, the surface of the waters glowing faintly with the dissolved battle of Early Living Marine Lifeforms. The scent of them lingered in the smoked, seared, and devoured.
Their residue now steeped the air in complexity and purity so concentrated that lesser beings might suffocate!
Seated at the heart of it all was Noah!
His upper body lay bare against the glimmering sands, the sharp lines of his body carved in living starlight.
Around him, tendrils of multicolored Living Existential Authority coiled and writhed like serpents.
And Noah, seated in stillness, remained with his eyes closed.
Until it came.
BOOOOM!
A booming ringing! Like a temple bell ringing across the span of existence itself tolling in recognition. A low, cavernous reverberation rolled through the Veiled Shore!
And from Noah’s seated figure...something rose.
A titanic structure burst into manifestation around him- blinding cerulean light arching into form with such reverent majesty that even the horizon bent to accommodate it.
The Early Sacred Living Infinity Tower of Osmont!

chapters.title: Chapter 3897: Foundation II
paragraphs: A glorious Tower, enacted by an Early Creature!

The base of the tower was simple- primal, as if the very concept of ’tower’ had been born from its likeness. Spiraling etchings crawled up its side in curving arcs, each inscribed with unending infinity symbols, each line seeming alive.
The Tower was supported not by stone or foundation, but by nine Eidolons.
Nine archaic, ancient figures made of pearlescent cerulean shells and etched bone armament- each one a towering Sacred Living Eidolon of Infinity.
Their forms were draped in woven moss and plates of translucent armor derived from the shattered husks of Mythic Living True Signatures.
Each Eidolon bore a different pose.
One knelt, palms flat on the sands, head bowed.
Another stood with one arm raised, as if bearing the weight of Wheels
One leaned upon the tower as if he alone supported it on his back.
Together, they upheld the tower with silent devotion, their bodies locked in ancient positions that sang of burden, memory, and quintessential labor.
Above them, the Tower pulsed softly.

From its peak, streams of white-gold and cerulean mist poured into the sky. There were no windows, no obvious openings, only a singular spiral staircase carved into its inner wall, rising and falling endlessly, as if even the architecture refused to admit a top or a bottom.
The Tower stood gloriously.
It was the crystallized proof of his will, of the blood of an Early Creature finally manifesting its might into form.
And this...was only the first.

The streams of white-gold and pale blue drifting above the peak of the tower coalesced with meticulous purpose. They twined and thickened, swirling inward to form a singular structure- dazzling in its geometry and hue. It was a structure of cerulean-gold, its form veinous and alive, as if arteries of power pulsed beneath its translucent shell.
A vessel like structure formed at the top of the Tower!
|The Early Sacred Living Infinity Tower of Osmont has formed the First Vein of an Early Creature, from which the Heart of an Early Creature can begin being forged from.|
He breathed. Only his breath, steady and slow, carried meaning now. His eyes opened just slightly- slits of molten gold and blue currently and infinity swirled within them.
|You have discovered new Records of the Weavings of Early Creatures as you pioneer your own path tracing back through the Earliest Folds.|

|In the Earliest Folds, Early Creatures cultivated Early Living Marine Lifeforms and reared Early Living Land Lifeforms, alongside harvesting Early Living Sacred Herbs in their Shores. They had an overabundance of resources filled with Complexity and Purity, which they utilized to forge their Glyphs and elevate their power. In this current era, such resources are exceedingly rare. Forging the Heart of an Early Creature will be immensely difficult.|
His fingers closed into the sand, feeling the granules break between his knuckles like brittle fragments of time.
"So..." he murmured, the syllable barely brushing past his lips. "They lived in abundance."
He tilted his chin slightly, eyes narrowing at the information unfurling like sacred scripture before him.
Abundance! He had Abundance. Even if it might not be enough!
"The Heart, formed only through Veins. The Veins, created by the Towers. Towers... birthed from complexity and corpses of the ancient marine life I consume..."
Marine Lifeforms, Land Lifeforms, Sacred Herbs!
Early Creatures had many things in abundance, and he did not. Yet his path was similar to theirs.
He breathed again, deeper this time.

It meant the path forward was slow and costly. To attain even the foundation of what the Early Creatures once were, he needed what they had freely- oceans teeming with life, forests of Sacred Herbs, and mountains of purity.
But he was not born in their age.
He would have to forge what they had for himself!
More prompts came down in this momentus occasion.

|You have unlocked the first stage of your Early Sacred Living Tower. The Tower of Osmont has begun aiding in the construction of the Heart of an Early Creature in the limited capacity of its first stage.|

|Taking your Tower to the Second Stage will allow it to be manifested as a Sacred Tower Totem in your Early Veiled Shore, with such a totem capable of attracting Early Living Land Lifeforms who can generate essential products that accelerate the progression of the Tower and other components of an Early Creature.|

|Stages of an Early Sacred Living Tower|:: 1- The Foundation Vein: The initial manifestation. Forms the First Vein. 2- The Sacred Totem: Allows manifestation of the Tower within the Early Veiled Shore as a Totem. Enables attraction of Early Living Land Lifeforms. 3- The Vital Lighthouse: Undefined 4- The Sovereign Pillar: Undefined. 5- Unknown: Undefined. 6- Unknown- Complete harmony with the Early Veiled Shore...
Grandiosity bloomed before him.
Each line carved itself into his memory like scripture. His gaze sharpened.
The newly built tower....had stages to it!
It was freshly built as it could become much more.

The second stage alone, The Sacred Totem, would allow the Tower to become a beacon. A living monument within his Early Veiled Shore. More than that, it would act as a call. A totem that would attract Early Living Land Lifeforms- creatures whose very breath and secretions would accelerate his forging of his Towers and the Heart.
He could imagine it already, those creatures wandering his Shore, their mere presence feeding his progression.
"Hmm...!" It was a beautiful scene just to think of!
The more the Heart was forged, the more his body would produce the mythical Blood of an Early Creature!
His eyes burned with desire.
He loved these kinds of things the most!
Learning about wonders he did not even know existed!
His infinite path...was proceeding smoothly.
But the question came as he progressed.
What would it take?
The next prompt gave him his answer.

|To advance the Early Sacred Living Infinity Tower of Osmont to its second stage: the Sacred Totem, you must consume the Sacred Bodies of 50 Early Living Marine Lifeforms, dedicating every part of them to the formation of the Tower. Alternatively, you may utilize treasures and resources that will be automatically evaluated and quantified in relation to the Sacred Bodies of Early Living Marine Lifeforms.|
HUUM!
He did not sigh at the difficulty.
He sighed at the truth.
"Fifty."
Fifty entire sacred bodies- purity, complexity, spirit, and matter, all poured into this one single Tower.
And that was just the second stage.
Noah leaned his head back, strands of vibrant hair slipping across his neck and shoulder as he exhaled.
His Glyph of the Protagonist spun slowly on his forehead, parsing the meaning and ramifications of every line. He needed...treasures. Caches. Everything.
Hannibal’s Loot.
Torus’s.
The burning spoils left by the Inevitabilities.
He had them. But even that was only enough for this one Tower, for Infinity. The others sat dormant, their growth proceeding slowly, waiting for the fullness of sacrifice.
He had already entirely finished the goldfish thst was the first Marine Lifeform to come!
Now, he needed a lot more.
Resources.
Treasures.
Time.
The path of an Early Creature was not for those afraid of cost.
And he...he would pay the price regardless of what it took!
