chapters.title: Chapter 3907: Glorious! III
paragraphs: A Sacred Totem had formed, and it flashed its brilliance gloriously!

|The Sacred Totem of Infinity awaits to have its Sacred Bell rang for the first time in order to release the call to Early Living Land Lifeforms. Chances of attraction are exceedingly low. The likelihood of summoning an Early Living Land Lifeform increases depending on the distinction of the Sacred Totem. Unique conceptual foundations significantly improve rarity and response rate.|
Noah stared at the prompt, lips curling faintly as he was ready to get started!
"Ring the Sacred Bell of Infinity," he commanded.
And...!
Silence.
|The Sacred Bell of a Sacred Totem can only be rang physically with the hands of the Early Creature.|
Noah exhaled slowly, his smile becoming sharp.
So that was how it had to be.

He approached, steps echoing softly as he reached the newly born tower. The base held a staircase spiraling upward along the interior wall, illuminated with glowing etchings that pulsed with every footfall. Moiraine, Liora, even Ruination anf others watched from below, silent reverence in their eyes. To them, this was no casual act, and instead something else entirely!

Each step bore weight. Not metaphorical- actual resistance pushed against him as if the tower itself tested his resolve. His body ached from the climb, yet his mind remained crystalline, focused. Complexity bloomed in his bones, each movement actually making him stronger, each breath another step in the ascent.
He reached the summit soon enough as...
The bell loomed before him.

Close up, it glowed faintly with swirling stellar wheels trapped within its curves. Beside it, a rope of woven cerulean threads and silver anchors waited for his touch. He reached out with one hand, then paused- and then both hands wrapped around it, and instantly...resistance struck.
As if he could not pull this rope down!

The Glyph of Infinity on his chest flashed. Then, the Glyph of the Protagonist pulsed. Muscles trembled, arms flexing as he pulled down with everything he was. The rope moved slowly, infinitely heavy!
And then...!
DING!
It rang.
A singular tone.
Deep.
Endless.
It reverberated through the folds of the Early Veiled Shore, through the sands, through the water, through the stillness! A sound older than sound, more profound than truth!
|The Sacred Bell of Infinity has been rung for the first time. An incredible achievement! From its ringing, immense waves of complexity erupt as another Glyph of Infinity is forming within you.|
Blue shockwaves spread from the bell tower’s peak, washing over the entire shore.
Below, Moiraine lifted her gaze. His mother and wives, too! And beyond, the Infiniverse and Ruination paused what they were doing, gazing upward as their bodies glowed faintly.
Another prompt bloomed.

|All those who hear the ringing of the Sacred Bell of Infinity, regardless of their power or complexity, will experience a single Early Sacred Living Epiphany that will either allow their complexity to surge by 25%, or broaden their weavings of complexity by incorporating the heavy musings of Infinity into what they are.|
HUUM!
Noah’s eyes narrowed, watching as glyphs of soft cerulean appeared above each of their heads- symbols wrapped in cloud-like halos as if the land itself had offered them a vision.
And still, the bell rang.
|The tolling of the bell has been deemed to be... Exceptional!|
Another prompt shimmered before his eyes.

|The bell has been rung, and depending on the myriad of factors of the Sacred Totem of Infinity, an Early Living Land Lifeform may be attracted... or may not be attracted. It may not be rung again for some time.|
He stood in the stillness of that final toll, the wind pressing against him at the tower’s peak. The sea remained silent. The skies seemed to hold their breath.
And Noah Osmont, Early Creature of the Budding Veiled Shore, simply waited.
He did not need to hope.
He had already done all he could!
The wait.

The tolling of the Sacred Bell of Infinity echoed long after its chime had faded, reverberating like a question cast into the breathless silence of the Early Veiled Shore. Noah stood atop the tower still, the cerulean Glyph of Infinity etched across the left side of his crystalline chest pulsing like a quiet star.
The air held its breath. The winds of the Veiled Shore dared not stir. And Noah waited.
Waiting- such a strange, neglected virtue!
A thing scorned by the impatient, misunderstood by the impulsive.
Yet to Noah, it was neither shameful nor passive. He knew that many were addicted to the immediacy of fire, to the flash of power and sudden culmination.
No one knew how to wait anymore. But waiting, truly waiting, was its own kind of strength. In waiting, one revealed whether they could bear the weight of their desire without drowning in it.
In waiting, one measured their stillness and strength by anticipation.
For the patient, sometimes...a second was enough.
BOOM!
A sound thundered through the thick, ever-churning mists that framed the borders of the Early Veiled Shore.
Noah turned his gaze toward it, his expression unreadable. A new prompt formed before his eyes, glowing cerulean!

|In the Earliest Folds, it was common for Early Creatures to wait days, months, even years after tolling the bell of their Sacred Totems before any Early Living Land Lifeform would answer. Yet for some... mere seconds sufficed. It all depended on the sweetness of the Bell’s call.|
|The ringing of the Sacred Totem of Infinity has been deemed unfathomably exceptional. An Early Living Land Lifeform has responded. Will you grant it entry?|
Noah’s lips curled into a smile. "Yes."
The mists trembled again.
BOOM!

A beam of white light surged forward from the gray mists- so bright, even the cerulean glow of the Sacred Totem seemed to dim in reverence. The radiance took form, and then form took shape. What emerged was not some titanous beast, nor a celestial horror.
No, what emerged... was a goat.
A goat!
But not just any goat.
It trotted through the mist as if it parted before its will, its steps soft and deliberate, its hooves clicking gently upon the grainy golden sand.

Its coat shimmered with such pureness of white it threatened blindness to all who stared too long. Each strand of its fur glowed like liquid snowlight, its eyes crystalline pools of ancient clarity. Yet those eyes... they narrowed. Sharpened.
Arrogance shimmered within them like a well-polished mirror!
Endless arrogance!

sentences.text: A Sacred Totem had formed, and it flashed its brilliance gloriously!
|The Sacred Totem of Infinity awaits to have its Sacred Bell rang for the first time in order to release the call to Early Living Land Lifeforms.
Chances of attraction are exceedingly low.
The likelihood of summoning an Early Living Land Lifeform increases depending on the distinction of the Sacred Totem.
Unique conceptual foundations significantly improve rarity and response rate.|
Noah stared at the prompt, lips curling faintly as he was ready to get started!
"Ring the Sacred Bell of Infinity," he commanded.
And...!
Silence.
|The Sacred Bell of a Sacred Totem can only be rang physically with the hands of the Early Creature.|
Noah exhaled slowly, his smile becoming sharp.
So that was how it had to be.
He approached, steps echoing softly as he reached the newly born tower.
The base held a staircase spiraling upward along the interior wall, illuminated with glowing etchings that pulsed with every footfall.
Moiraine, Liora, even Ruination anf others watched from below, silent reverence in their eyes.
To them, this was no casual act, and instead something else entirely!
Each step bore weight.
Not metaphorical- actual resistance pushed against him as if the tower itself tested his resolve.
His body ached from the climb, yet his mind remained crystalline, focused.
Complexity bloomed in his bones, each movement actually making him stronger, each breath another step in the ascent.
He reached the summit soon enough as...
The bell loomed before him.
Close up, it glowed faintly with swirling stellar wheels trapped within its curves.
Beside it, a rope of woven cerulean threads and silver anchors waited for his touch.
He reached out with one hand, then paused- and then both hands wrapped around it, and instantly...resistance struck.
As if he could not pull this rope down!
The Glyph of Infinity on his chest flashed.
Then, the Glyph of the Protagonist pulsed.
Muscles trembled, arms flexing as he pulled down with everything he was.
The rope moved slowly, infinitely heavy!
And then...!
DING!
It rang.
A singular tone.
Deep.
Endless.
It reverberated through the folds of the Early Veiled Shore, through the sands, through the water, through the stillness!
A sound older than sound, more profound than truth!
|The Sacred Bell of Infinity has been rung for the first time.
An incredible achievement!
From its ringing, immense waves of complexity erupt as another Glyph of Infinity is forming within you.|
Blue shockwaves spread from the bell tower’s peak, washing over the entire shore.
Below, Moiraine lifted her gaze.
His mother and wives, too!
And beyond, the Infiniverse and Ruination paused what they were doing, gazing upward as their bodies glowed faintly.
Another prompt bloomed.

|All those who hear the ringing of the Sacred Bell of Infinity, regardless of their power or complexity, will experience a single Early Sacred Living Epiphany that will either allow their complexity to surge by 25%, or broaden their weavings of complexity by incorporating the heavy musings of Infinity into what they are.|
HUUM!
Noah’s eyes narrowed, watching as glyphs of soft cerulean appeared above each of their heads- symbols wrapped in cloud-like halos as if the land itself had offered them a vision.
And still, the bell rang.
|The tolling of the bell has been deemed to be...
Exceptional!|
Another prompt shimmered before his eyes.
|The bell has been rung, and depending on the myriad of factors of the Sacred Totem of Infinity, an Early Living Land Lifeform may be attracted... or may not be attracted.
It may not be rung again for some time.|
He stood in the stillness of that final toll, the wind pressing against him at the tower’s peak.
The sea remained silent.
The skies seemed to hold their breath.
And Noah Osmont, Early Creature of the Budding Veiled Shore, simply waited.
He did not need to hope.
He had already done all he could!
The wait.
The tolling of the Sacred Bell of Infinity echoed long after its chime had faded, reverberating like a question cast into the breathless silence of the Early Veiled Shore.
Noah stood atop the tower still, the cerulean Glyph of Infinity etched across the left side of his crystalline chest pulsing like a quiet star.
The air held its breath.
The winds of the Veiled Shore dared not stir.
And Noah waited.
Waiting- such a strange, neglected virtue!
A thing scorned by the impatient, misunderstood by the impulsive.
Yet to Noah, it was neither shameful nor passive.
He knew that many were addicted to the immediacy of fire, to the flash of power and sudden culmination.

chapters.title: Chapter 3908: Glorious! IV
paragraphs: The goat moved with the casual superiority of a sovereign among lesser beings. Its gaze flicked over the figures gathered along the Shore.
It scoffed at the Emperor Penguin.
Snorted at the crouched forms of other Existences here!
It passed Moiraine, and for a moment, its proud expression eased into something approaching approval. It gave a tiny nod, as if saying, "You, at least, know your worth."

It reached Ruination and the Infiniverse- two pillars of burgeoning power- and for them, the goat’s eyes gleamed as it gave a regal nod of respect. But that arrogance remained. It was not a creature interested in flattery!
Its attention fixed forward, to the tower.
The goat came to a halt before the Sacred Totem of Infinity, its crystalline eyes lifting to meet Noah’s. It said nothing. Yet its expression said everything- the bell had been acceptable!
More than acceptable!
HUUM!
With something bordering on bliss, it nudged the blue-gleaming tower walls, letting out a soft, self-satisfied grunt.
|The Eminent Early Living Land Lifeform, Heidrun, has answered the call and arrived at the Early Veiled Shore.|
|Land Lifeforms are categorized by rarity: Basic, Refined, Eminent, and Kleos.|
Noah’s eyebrows lifted. Eminent.

He leapt from the peak of the tower, descending like a star trailing darkness and starlight. He landed gently before the goat, who tilted its head upward, meeting his gaze with that same imperious expression.
He smiled as waves of information bloomed!
|Name: Heidrun
Designation: Eminent Early Living Land Lifeform
Rarity: Eminent

Lineage: Ancestral Echoes of Yrdifrost Lore: In the lost and earliest Chapters of the Folds, Heidrun was revered by Early Creatures as a terrifying conduit of nourishment. Her kind were rare beyond measure, said to dwell near the Loom where Totems gathered in reverent silence. The appearance of even one Heidrun would send shockwaves through Early Creatures. Entire Domains would offer up Marine Lifeforms, Early Sacred Herbs, and other Land Lifeforms to trade for one. The Reason was for....The Sacred Mead of Existence.

Sacred Mead of Existence: Heidrun can produce a golden-white mead imbued with the distilled essences of Complexity and Purity. One sip fortifies the soul, purifies the body, elevates existence, and enhances the forging of any weavings related to Early Creatures by an unquantifiable amount for the next day. Its effect on those lesser than Early Creature is so profound that having more than a drop can be deadly...
Existential Infusion: When near Early Creatures, Heidrun’s aura causes their internal Hearts or Existence to experience accelerated refinement.
Passive Boon – Glorious Stubbornness: Immune to all forms of compulsion and influence. Will only respond to those it deems "sufficiently majestic."
Disposition: Arrogant. Discerning. Prideful. Loyal only to those it deems worthy.|
Noah slowly exhaled. His gaze lingered on the words "sufficiently majestic" for longer than necessary.
The goat... Heidrun, huffed. Her nostrils flared in response, the arrogance in her expression somehow intensifying.
He chuckled.
"Welcome to the Early Veiled Shore," he said, voice smooth and resonant, his tone carrying the full gravity of someone who bore the burden of dominion.
The goat said nothing. Merely lowered her head. And with unspoken grace... stayed.
The first Sacred Totem had been tolled. The first Land Lifeform had answered!
The Early Veiled Shore... was no longer merely budding. It was beginning to blossom!
The bell’s toll still echoed softly, diffused across the sands and mist of the Early Veiled Shore like a hymn from another time.
And in that fading chime, Noah and the goat stood face to face.
Neither moved.

The goat, resplendent in its arrogance, gleamed under the blue light of the Sacred Totem. Its pure white coat shimmered with a terrifying luster, and its head was held high, nose tilted upward, eyes half-lidded with the judgment of a creature that had seen kingdoms rise and fall and found them all wanting. It looked at him as if he were some passing curiosity.
Noah... merely smiled. Calculated, amused, and infinitely patient.

He glanced at the glowing panel that hovered before him, filled with glorious script and glorious revelations. The Sacred Mead of Existence, a liquid sought after even in the Earliest Folds. That was what he desired right now!
"Produce some Sacred Mead for me," he said simply.
And...!
There was a pause.

The goat blinked. Its pupils were as clear as quartz, cold and unbothered. Then, almost comically, it turned its head toward the tower behind it with a look that could only be interpreted as baffled offense.
Can you believe this guy?
Then came the haughty huff.
And another prompt.
|To obtain Sacred Mead of Existence from the Early Living Land Lifeform: Heidrun, one must hand milk it directly from its glorious udders.|
Noah blinked.
The goat shifted proudly, displaying its side. It was offering access, yes- but it made its expectations clear. If he wanted the Sacred Mead of Existence, he’d have to put in the work!
Noah chuckled at this surreal reality!
He turned, voice slightly louder. "Someone get me a bucket!"

There was a moment of stunned silence, the sound of shuffling feet, and then the elegant form of Moiraine approached. She held a crystal-clear Glass Bucket delicately in both hands, her voice composed, tone resolute.
"Sir," she said with practiced calm, "this is beneath your station. Let me handle it."
Her poise was the kind of thing that made existence listen. But Heidrun’s eyes narrowed.
The moment Moiraine stepped near, the goat snorted.

A violent gust erupted from its nose, a blast of concentrated complexity that caught Moiraine full in the chest and sent her flying backward, her body tumbling across the sand and into the lapping edges of the shore.
BOOM!
Gasps rang out, but Moiraine merely rose from the shallows with wet hair and narrowed eyes. She looked back toward Heidrun with startled respect. She wasn’t angry, only intrigued and shocked!

|The Early Living Land Lifeform: Heidrun possesses the Quality of Glorious Stubbornness. It is Immune to all forms of compulsion or influence and will only respond to those it deems sufficiently majestic.|
Moiraine...was not deemed sufficiently majestic!
She jumped up and appeared beside Noah again, wiping the dampness from her brow. She offered him the bucket solemnly and seriously. "Sir, please.
He took it.
He set it gently beneath the goat, who now seemed positively glowing with satisfaction.

With a sigh, Noah knelt upon the rising golden sand. The mound beneath him shaped itself softly to his weight. His bare chest reflected the tower’s glow, a crystalline sheen rippling across his form as his hand reached forward and grasped.
The udder was firm, warm.
And the moment he squeezed...
HUUM!
Golden liquid of unfathomable clarity gushed out in radiant arcs.

It filled the glass bucket with glowing swirls that looked less like milk and more like liquefied starlight. The scent of it struck immediately- a rich, honeyed aroma filled the air, thick with something more profound than sweetness.
The atmosphere of the Early Veiled Shore changed.

The weight of the air grew denser. The Towers of Origin within every being present began to hum. Complexity surged. Purity twined in elegant spirals. The very weavings of existence thickened with each drop that fell!
The concentration was so terrifying that in the next moment...
PAH! PAH!

Kazuhiko, the Emperor Penguin, Liora, and many others lost consciousness as their bodies fell down onto the sand, their existences unable to handle the terrifying concentration of the Sacred Mead of Existence!

chapters.title: Chapter 3909: Glorious V
paragraphs: Many were knocked unconscious!
Of those that remained awake, their Existence buzzed as their complexity and purity exploded upwards in a somewhat controlled manner!
Instantly, a second Basic Early Living Existential Glyph of Ruination began to form on the body of Ruination.

On the Infiniverse, an unknown reaction seemed to occuring with her as like blooming singularities, the Basic Early Living Existential Glyphs of Manadynamics, Continuity, and Dreams all bloomed simultaneously- her eyes vibrating with terrifying brilliance as one must not forget...the Early Veiled Shore...was locaded within her.
In her center.
Literally.
So what would it mean for her when the Early Veiled Shore continued to unlock its wonders?
Moiraine almost dropped to her knees on the side as her entire existence felt like it was quivering, her already tremendous complexity and purity...shockingly rising faster than it ever had before.
Her eyes trembled as within their depths, she could not help but howl out against the foolishness of Diviticus and her Mentor!
How foolish were they to have actually gone against this being?!
HUUM!
The bucket shone.
So did the eyes of those shocked who remained conscious as the shocking process seemed to just be getting started!
Noah kept milking as he mads sure his Mother, Son, Adelaide, and all others were okay.
He then stared at Heidrun with quiet wonder. "Where do you come from?" he asked calmly. "Do you know where others like you dwell? Do you know where the Early Creatures might still be?"
Heidrun shimmered, its arrogant eyes lazing around.
The goat’s only response was a dignified snort.
A new prompt answered him instead.
|Very little additional records can be obtained regarding the origins of the Early Living Land Lifeform, Heidrun, at this moment.|
He nodded.
It figured.
The milk flowed. The Sacred Mead of Existence flowed!
Until...
BZZT!
Noah blinked.
The udder resisted his grasp. Heidrun stepped back with a final, triumphant shake of her glimmering coat. Her eyes gleamed. Then she turned and began to trot away.
|Heidrun has produced as much Sacred Mead of Existence as she desires at this time. If you wish to collect more in the future, present her with her favorite delicacy.|
Noah remained sitting, the golden bucket pulsing before him. Heidrun strutted away, her expression smug, tail flicking with casual power as she returned to bask beneath the Sacred Totem’s glow.
He stared after her, shaking his head.
Then, he laughed!
It slipped out slow and full. His smile widened, eyes lifting to the skies as the breeze kissed his face.
"You know," he said quietly, to no one and everyone, "I’ve always wanted to be a farmer."
HUUM!
And for the briefest moment in the folds of existence, under a sparkling sky and upon golden sand that pulsed with ancestral might, Noah Osmont felt as if he truly were...a farmer.
All it required was to find and unlock the wonder that was the Early Veiled Shore!
The bucket of Sacred Mead of Existence glowed faintly where it sat in the golden sands, its surface calm and still, as if aware of its own impossible worth.
Noah’s gaze remained locked on it, his expression unreadable but deeply contemplative.
Unimaginably contemplative!
Around him, the sand of the Early Veiled Shore shifted softly, humming with an unseen rhythm, and below his bare feet, he could feel the tremor of something glorious moving.
Inside his being, Towers began to shudder.
A subtle quake of acceleration.

The early Towers of Osmont that would have taken a great deal of to form a single vein or layer now pulsed with progress. More than that, deep within the core of his existence, the Ventryalis, the Primal Root Atrium of Echoes, moved.
It had been crawling before.
Crawling despite everything he’d done, despite all the complexity he’d built, all the purity he’d burned through!
Now, it surged...just from him breathing the scent released by the Sacred Mead of Existence!
Every second, his Ventryalis inched forward in its completion, as if the golden milk in that bucket was reaching into him, humming softly to the rhythm of something quintessential!
And he hadn’t even tasted it yet.
Around this time...
BOOM!
The air above the Early Veiled Shore rippled.
Noah’s eyes lifted, glazed with distant starlight as he turned his gaze toward the faraway battlefield, where he could sense it- faintly but clearly.
The clash between Living Origins and Living Paradoxes in the Nullvein Gravewake Folds.
A silent war, loud only to those whose perception could reach across threads of Existence.
His voice was quiet, low, more to himself than anyone around him, but heavy with thought.
But Moiraine listened in her stupor and fascination.
Any others who could listen, listened.
"There is...a strange cruelty to the weavings of Existence," he murmured, contemplative!

"A war wages not far from here. A war of truths and contradictions, of beings locked in endless opposition. They struggle, bleed, scream with purpose, chasing absolutes. And yet, here... here, something unimaginable has bloomed quietly..."
HUUM!
His existence buzzed with unknown epiphanies as his complexity and purity surged!
While Living Paradoxes and Living Origins hurl their authority and philosophy at one another, they cannot see it. Perhaps they never would!
Life moved differently for many. Some beings run, some stand still.
Some, like Noah, walked into forgotten places!
He didn’t win a war or claim a throne to have what he had now. He simply made a series of choices... to seek. To wander. And somehow, that led him here.
His eyes were unimaginably bright as his voice echoed out, mainly to himself.
"Sometimes, what matters most is simply where we choose to stop walking."
WAA!
His hand gripped the handle of the bucket.
"If only...they could understand that."
The Sacred Mead pulsed with light, the milky golden liquid shimmering like starlit honey. Just the scent of it, just the nearness, had propelled his Towers forward.
What would a taste do?
He lifted the bucket slowly. It felt heavier than its size should allow. An existential weight, not a physical one.
Then, with the silence of inevitability, he drank.
A gulp.
Roughly...two hundred droplets of the Sacred Mead of Existence slid down his throat.
And...
Oh!
BOOM!
The air bent around him.
His body jerked with such violent force that a ripple of golden and cerulean light burst out in all directions!
Only his status as an Early Creature kept his frame from disintegrating outright. Even still, he staggered half a step, and a low exhale escaped his lips.
He was burning.
Gloriously burning with multicolored, and yet dull, archaic light!
He was ascending!
Within him...

|The Ventryalis – The Primal Root Atrium of Echoes, the first part of the Heart of an Early Creature, is going towards a glorious completion from the exposure to the droplets of the Sacred Mead of Existence.|
|A Profound and Quintessential change is occurring within your existence due to the consumption of something unimaginably complex.|
|81 Drops of Blood of an Early Creature have been generated in the Ventryalis!|
|162 Drops of Blood of an Early Creature have been generated in the Ventryalis!!|
|324 Drops of Blood of an Early Creature have been generated in the Ventryalis!!!|
His heart...it was forming!
The Heart of an Early Creature, a beating construct of power, of lineage, of age.
The air changed.
HUUM!
An old sound. A trembling weight passed through the folds of the Early Veiled Shore. All life paused!
Moiraine stepped back, breath caught in her throat!
Even Heidrun, the arrogant goat whose pride exceeded the sky, turned toward him.
She stared at Noah in silence.
And then, finally- nodded.
Affirmation.
As if to say, yes.
Now you are beginning to become what you were always meant to be. What you should be!
The aura of age swelled from Noah like thunder without sound, like stars being born in the lungs of a dead universe! Like Omniverses being born in dry frequencies of the Wheel!
And it did not stop.
Oh, it did not stop!

sentences.text: Many were knocked unconscious!
Of those that remained awake, their Existence buzzed as their complexity and purity exploded upwards in a somewhat controlled manner!
Instantly, a second Basic Early Living Existential Glyph of Ruination began to form on the body of Ruination.

On the Infiniverse, an unknown reaction seemed to occuring with her as like blooming singularities, the Basic Early Living Existential Glyphs of Manadynamics, Continuity, and Dreams all bloomed simultaneously- her eyes vibrating with terrifying brilliance as one must not forget...the Early Veiled Shore...was locaded within her.
In her center.
Literally.
So what would it mean for her when the Early Veiled Shore continued to unlock its wonders?
Moiraine almost dropped to her knees on the side as her entire existence felt like it was quivering, her already tremendous complexity and purity...shockingly rising faster than it ever had before.
Her eyes trembled as within their depths, she could not help but howl out against the foolishness of Diviticus and her Mentor!
How foolish were they to have actually gone against this being?!
HUUM!
The bucket shone.
So did the eyes of those shocked who remained conscious as the shocking process seemed to just be getting started!
Noah kept milking as he mads sure his Mother, Son, Adelaide, and all others were okay.
He then stared at Heidrun with quiet wonder.
"Where do you come from?" he asked calmly.
"Do you know where others like you dwell?
Do you know where the Early Creatures might still be?"
Heidrun shimmered, its arrogant eyes lazing around.
The goat’s only response was a dignified snort.
A new prompt answered him instead.
|Very little additional records can be obtained regarding the origins of the Early Living Land Lifeform, Heidrun, at this moment.|
He nodded.
It figured.
The milk flowed.
The Sacred Mead of Existence flowed!
Until...
BZZT!
Noah blinked.
The udder resisted his grasp.
Heidrun stepped back with a final, triumphant shake of her glimmering coat.
Her eyes gleamed.
Then she turned and began to trot away.
|Heidrun has produced as much Sacred Mead of Existence as she desires at this time.
If you wish to collect more in the future, present her with her favorite delicacy.|
Noah remained sitting, the golden bucket pulsing before him.
Heidrun strutted away, her expression smug, tail flicking with casual power as she returned to bask beneath the Sacred Totem’s glow.
He stared after her, shaking his head.
Then, he laughed!
It slipped out slow and full.
His smile widened, eyes lifting to the skies as the breeze kissed his face.
"You know," he said quietly, to no one and everyone, "I’ve always wanted to be a farmer."
HUUM!
And for the briefest moment in the folds of existence, under a sparkling sky and upon golden sand that pulsed with ancestral might, Noah Osmont felt as if he truly were...a farmer.
All it required was to find and unlock the wonder that was the Early Veiled Shore!
The bucket of Sacred Mead of Existence glowed faintly where it sat in the golden sands, its surface calm and still, as if aware of its own impossible worth.
Noah’s gaze remained locked on it, his expression unreadable but deeply contemplative.
Unimaginably contemplative!
Around him, the sand of the Early Veiled Shore shifted softly, humming with an unseen rhythm, and below his bare feet, he could feel the tremor of something glorious moving.
Inside his being, Towers began to shudder.
A subtle quake of acceleration.
The early Towers of Osmont that would have taken a great deal of to form a single vein or layer now pulsed with progress.
More than that, deep within the core of his existence, the Ventryalis, the Primal Root Atrium of Echoes, moved.
It had been crawling before.
Crawling despite everything he’d done, despite all the complexity he’d built, all the purity he’d burned through!
Now, it surged...just from him breathing the scent released by the Sacred Mead of Existence!
Every second, his Ventryalis inched forward in its completion, as if the golden milk in that bucket was reaching into him, humming softly to the rhythm of something quintessential!
And he hadn’t even tasted it yet.
Around this time...
BOOM!
The air above the Early Veiled Shore rippled.
Noah’s eyes lifted, glazed with distant starlight as he turned his gaze toward the faraway battlefield, where he could sense it- faintly but clearly.
The clash between Living Origins and Living Paradoxes in the Nullvein Gravewake Folds.
A silent war, loud only to those whose perception could reach across threads of Existence.
His voice was quiet, low, more to himself than anyone around him, but heavy with thought.
But Moiraine listened in her stupor and fascination.
Any others who could listen, listened.
"There is...a strange cruelty to the weavings of Existence," he murmured, contemplative!
"A war wages not far from here.
A war of truths and contradictions, of beings locked in endless opposition.
They struggle, bleed, scream with purpose, chasing absolutes.
And yet, here... here, something unimaginable has bloomed quietly..."
HUUM!
His existence buzzed with unknown epiphanies as his complexity and purity surged!
While Living Paradoxes and Living Origins hurl their authority and philosophy at one another, they cannot see it.
Perhaps they never would!
Life moved differently for many.
Some beings run, some stand still.
Some, like Noah, walked into forgotten places!
He didn’t win a war or claim a throne to have what he had now.
He simply made a series of choices... to seek.
To wander.
And somehow, that led him here.
His eyes were unimaginably bright as his voice echoed out, mainly to himself.
"Sometimes, what matters most is simply where we choose to stop walking."
WAA!
His hand gripped the handle of the bucket.
"If only...they could understand that."
The Sacred Mead pulsed with light, the milky golden liquid shimmering like starlit honey.
Just the scent of it, just the nearness, had propelled his Towers forward.
What would a taste do?
He lifted the bucket slowly.
It felt heavier than its size should allow.
An existential weight, not a physical one.
Then, with the silence of inevitability, he drank.
A gulp.
Roughly...two hundred droplets of the Sacred Mead of Existence slid down his throat.
And...
Oh!
BOOM!
The air bent around him.
His body jerked with such violent force that a ripple of golden and cerulean light burst out in all directions!
Only his status as an Early Creature kept his frame from disintegrating outright.
Even still, he staggered half a step, and a low exhale escaped his lips.
He was burning.
Gloriously burning with multicolored, and yet dull, archaic light!
He was ascending!
Within him...

|The Ventryalis – The Primal Root Atrium of Echoes, the first part of the Heart of an Early Creature, is going towards a glorious completion from the exposure to the droplets of the Sacred Mead of Existence.|
|A Profound and Quintessential change is occurring within your existence due to the consumption of something unimaginably complex.|
|81 Drops of Blood of an Early Creature have been generated in the Ventryalis!|
|162 Drops of Blood of an Early Creature have been generated in the Ventryalis!!|
|324 Drops of Blood of an Early Creature have been generated in the Ventryalis!!!|
His heart...it was forming!
The Heart of an Early Creature, a beating construct of power, of lineage, of age.
The air changed.
HUUM!
An old sound.
A trembling weight passed through the folds of the Early Veiled Shore.
All life paused!
Moiraine stepped back, breath caught in her throat!
Even Heidrun, the arrogant goat whose pride exceeded the sky, turned toward him.
She stared at Noah in silence.
And then, finally- nodded.
Affirmation.
As if to say, yes.
Now you are beginning to become what you were always meant to be.
What you should be!
The aura of age swelled from Noah like thunder without sound, like stars being born in the lungs of a dead universe!
Like Omniverses being born in dry frequencies of the Wheel!
And it did not stop.
Oh, it did not stop!

chapters.title: Chapter 3910: Choices! I
paragraphs: How exactly did one quantify age or oldness?
Some would claim it came through wrinkles carved onto the flesh like glyphs, the slow decay of joints and bone, or the graying of hair kissed by countless suns.
Others would say that it was measured in experiences- a ledger of moments, some sweet, others shattering, that shaped the weight of one’s existence.
Others believed age was the accumulation of self-reflection, of pain endured with grace, of love accepted and lost, of wonder that never faded.
And some deeper beliefs would describe age as a layering of consciousness across dimensions, a story told not in years but in the evolution of understanding.
And then, there were those who knew age wasn’t a number at all, but a scent- musky and deep- or a gaze that saw you and every version of you, all at once.
Whatever it was, age was presence!
It was weight!
And in this moment, Noah Osmont- still, unwavering- gave off the feeling of age so deep it made the air dense.
On the sands of the Early Veiled Shore, golden light shimmered as if hesitant to drift too close.

He stood with the bucket still warm from his hand, the Sacred Mead of Existence quietly standing against its crystalline walls. His bare chest shone with a soft, ancient glow, and from beneath his skin, something pulsed.
Noah’s eyes were closed. And inward, he saw it.
The Ventryalis.
The Primal Root Atrium of Echoes.
It pulsed with solemnity, a chamber of silence and memory.
This was no ordinary part of a heart.
It resembled a chambered vault made from living obsidian vines, with glowing arteries that pulsed with multicolored light, threading outward in fractal branches like the roots of a celestial tree.
Its texture was both biological and mythical- fibers like the sinew of existence itself forming the atrial walls, while its floor resembled an endless spiral carved into living stone.
At its center, a bulbous node pulsed with a steady rhythm, each throb emitting pulses that sent soft echoes throughout Noah’s body, into the Towers of Osmont, into the glyphs shining along his bones.
It was complete.
A prompt bloomed before his closed eyes.
|The Ventryalis – The Primal Root Atrium of Echoes has been fully formed.|
|All systems within your existence are now accepting and digesting the Sacred Mead of Existence.|
|You can now freely generate 1 Drop of Blood of an Early Creature every minute.|

|You can now begin nurturing a Concept or Idea from your Towers of Osmont into your own True Absolute Existential Resistance, even before surpassing the Originus Venerant Realm as from this point forward, limitations based on Realm boundaries defined by Living Existences and those lesser than them no longer apply to you.|
The prompts were overwhelming.
And there were many as even now, they werent done!
|Due to the formation of the Ventryalis, the complexity of your existence, your Glyphs, Towers, and other Collective Factors, your strength has been assigned an Age.|
|Age Assigned: 1 / 1,000 |

|Note: The Age system for Early Creatures measures their authority, complexity, and presence relative to the foundational archetype of an Early Creature. An Age of 1 / 1,000 signifies a nascent but True status.|
Noah opened his eyes, the bucket still in hand, its golden milk reflecting a dancing starlight.
He smiled faintly.
He was given an age.
An age of an Early Creature!
And it turned out...he had not even reached 1 years old! He was a thousandth. 0.001!
This was fantastical and terrifying to think about as if Age was a measure of strength, how terrifying would Early Creatures be at this moment?
Would their Age continue rising with the passage of time, or if an Early Creature had their power stall at 100 years of age, even a million years later, they would still be 100 years of age?
There were too many unknowns as he couldn’t say for sure!
He sighed with power and solemnity as he also thought about the other boons just now obtained.
A completed Ventryalis. The generation of a Drop of Blood of an Early Creature a minute! The forging...of his own type of Resistance based off a Tower of Osmont!
There were many boons as others could not be seen individually and could only be observed collectively!
His vision changed once more as a summarized panel shimmered before him.
[Noah Osmont] (Early Creature – 810 Drops of Blood) Age: 1 / 1,000
|Early Living Existential Glyphs: Protagonist x1 (Basic), Infinity x5 (Basic)|
|Complexity Quotient (CQ): 18,225,000 (22,000,000) SU|
|Purity Quotient (PQ): 19,220,000 (23,000,000) SU|
|True Sources with Towers of Origin Constructed: 0|
|True Sources with Towers of Osmont Constructed: 6|
|Average Lattice Quantity Per Tower: 3,000,000+|
|Total Existential Dimensional Lattices: 455,000,000+|
|Collective Total Resistance: 1002%|
He exhaled slowly, setting the bucket beside him as his entire being- his blood, his breath, his very thoughts- began to align in silent, seismic shifts.
Within his chest, the Ventryalis pulsed as more and more systems synchronized with its ancient rhythm.
The forming Heart. The Early Atlas of the Folds. The Towers that stretched across the unseen weavings of his existence!
His Existence was growing more complex by the moment!
Time.
All he needed was time.
He had made his choices. Not rushed into endless battles. Not clawed up realms for validation. No, he chose to sit. To learn. To grow.
But growth...was never quiet.
HUUM!
The sound shuddered through the folds, subtle at first, then sweeping across the golden shore in a tangible pulse.
He lowered the bucket gently back to the sand.
|Another wave of Early Living Marine Lifeforms has been detected approaching the Early Veiled Shore. Their purpose remains the rectification of population discrepancy.|

On the distant shores where the sacred waters shimmered, new bubbles had begun to surface. Multicolored light arced across the surface in elegant weaves, and the murky depths below pulsed with forming life.
Noah turned toward Moiraine, who stood silently not far behind him. Her posture was one of steady poise, even though she was looking towards him with even greater awe!
His voice carried gently, but firmly.
"Moiraine. Could you see to that?"
Her head lifted, her shoulders straightened as she stepped forward.
"Yes, Sir."
Her eyes lingered a second too long, reverence gleaming in their depths. Then, she was gone, the sand barely disturbed beneath her feet.
Noah remained where he was.
Still.
Calm.
Time would carry the rest!
And as time flowed, so did the weavings of those entangled!

chapters.title: Chapter 3911: Choices! II
paragraphs: In the Nullvein Gravewake Folds.
Where once stood a Paradoxical Prison, there now churned a battlefield!

The ancient structure shattered like glass under the weight of too many truths contorted into lies. Now, the broken remnants of that prison framed a war of extremities as Living Paradoxes clashed with Living Origins.
And the Paradoxes were winning as they had sheer numbers- led by Oryzarakh!

Booming layers of twisted brilliance erupted from over a few dozen Paradoxes, each hurling immense Authority- Living Paradoxical weavings formed from hundreds of millions of Lattices. These strands undid everything in their path. They folded existence backward into the shape of confusion and doubt.
Amid this surreal deluge, a solitary light pushed against the tide. Vast. Glacial. Immense.
Vorellion.

The Ancient Living Turtle of Twelve Epochs braced its omniverse-spanning shell as nine of its heads drew in toward the center. Each of the nine bore their own radiant halos, every one layered with Purpose and Origin. As the deadly waves of Paradox neared, Vorellion’s voices murmured in unison!
HUUM!
"Begin No Purpose."
A wave pulsed outward.
From the convergence of its nine heads, an impossible paradox was unknit by refusal of premise.
The very concept of the Paradoxical attack was nullified, its purpose made retroactively void!
The Authority crashed... and vanished, as if it had never intended harm, as if it had never been born.
Its origin...was ended!
The pressure lifted. The Living Origins found breathing room again.
And Vorellion’s gaze, those nine deep orbs of ancient wisdom, settled upon the young Living Origin beside them. Once jailed in this forsaken Fold, now trembling and radiant with strength.
The thought burned through its minds.
How dare they? How dare these cruel, vile beings try to cage something so new?!
HUUM!
As Vorellion was thinking this.
An oppressive tide fell upon the battlefield.
A voice followed- low and simmering.
"I am thoroughly enraged. And in the past eon, I have not been enraged."
Vorellion froze. Its shell pulser. Every head recognized the pressure. The pressure of an Honored Living Paradox!
The Ancient Turtle’s power neared the threshold of Honored, but it was not there yet.
They had sent word for reinforcements of more Living Origins to this location. Some younger Living Origins had arrived already. But none strong enough.
Not yet!
Honored Gold’s arrival needed no fanfare.
The Fold itself grew silent.

He descended like a thought too heavy to hold, like light bent around him in apology. Wings and halos pulsed around him- countless, changing, contradicting. They were there and not there, infinite in number, yet none remained visible for more than a breath.
The Honored Living Golden Paradox floated forward. Calm. Cold.
His gaze swept over the battlefield. And then, settled.
"When," he asked, his tone clipped with condescension, "did the Living Origins grow balls?"
He looked faintly, with genuine malice.
"Do you seek more massacres in the Battlefront Folds?"
The Origins stirred.
Altheon flared! Shaynara surged! But none stepped forward.
"Distractions," Gold continued, flicking his wrist. "You are all distractions."
He tilted his head.
"And I detest distractions."
His voice dropped.
"Liar’s Paradox."
The Fold trembled.
The Liar’s Paradox!
It was a self-referential wound in logic. An example to better understand it...was the statement- "This sentence is false."
This sentance...is false.
If true, then it is false. If false, then it is true. A loop. A contradiction. A poison.
Gold shaped his own version of such a wonder!
"The Living Origins are only alive because they are already dead."
HUUM!
A terrifying statement was made.
Contradicting! Unfathomable!
And behind him, a golden Tower of Origin flickered- built to protect and to unravel. To enforce contradiction!
The Living Origins roared with a shocked sense of despair.
White towers erupted from behind the Living Origins in response!
But...a heartbeat later, they began to crumble.
Altheon watched comrades unravel. Shaynara screamed as she sought to hold on!
The faces of Origin turned to terror and disbelief as their essence cracked from within.
One Origin after another fell, their light snuffed by the unbearable contradiction of their own existence.
From the single statement filled with the complexity of Honored Gold!
An Honored Living Existence...was simply that powerful.
Only three remained.
Altheon. Shaynara. Vorellion.
And one more.
Bob.
The young one had not fallen in all this as one had to wonder...how?
Vorellion reeled from the massacre. Its heads shook. Each one dripping with sorrow!
It saw the perished Origins as it wanted to roar, but did not!
Then, with profound stillness, all nine heads turned to the sky.
"For my kin."
It did not roar.
It simply... gave.
And it gave everything with all its heart!
Origin surged. The echoes of its purpose, the very reason for its birth, flared one last time. And then...
"End!"
A pulse of Origin erupted as Vorellion unmade itself- from duty. As a sacrifice.
In its unraveling, a flare was released.
A Call!
A summons for an Honored Living Origin.
Gold watched the act with distaste.
"Pathetic," he said. His tone was dripping with disdain. "Some things are best left to end. There is peace in it. A clean fade. But you cling. You flail."
He raised a hand.
"Let me clean it up."
He reached for Altheon, who braced himself!
But then...
Gold paused.
His hand froze in midair.
His eyes narrowed.
His Authority recoiled as his expression became heavy!
"Form the Transcendent Paradoxical Tower of Inevitability!" he bellowed.
The Fold fractured as what he sensed came down, a terrifying musing of Origin manifesting!
White light descended like thunder on silk. An unmistakable brilliance.
A woman walked through the light.
Her legs emerged first, fair and radiant. Then her dress, a flowing garment of sparkling white, stitched with stellar jewels. Her hair, long and white, shimmered like the threads of destiny.
Her voice rang, clear and amused.
"Whatever could have pulled an Honored Living Paradox here?"
Gold’s expression soured as he sensed...
Royalty.
"Do the Living Origins have so many forces now that they send a Royal Living Origin to lesser Folds?"
The woman smiled.

"Royal Origin Calypso, at your service." she said sweetly, giving a curtsy no less regal for being unnecessary. "And yes. I came because someone here gave me good news about a little girl I thought dead"
Her gaze fell on Altheon.
"One of their bodies," she said, her voice soft as falling snow, "cannot perish."
And she smiled.
The Fold pulsed once more.
And the war reached a terrifying precipice!

He looked faintly, with genuine malice.
"Do you seek more massacres in the Battlefront Folds?"
The Origins stirred.
Altheon flared!
Shaynara surged!
But none stepped forward.
"Distractions," Gold continued, flicking his wrist.
"You are all distractions."
He tilted his head.
"And I detest distractions."
His voice dropped.
"Liar’s Paradox."
The Fold trembled.
The Liar’s Paradox!
It was a self-referential wound in logic.
An example to better understand it...was the statement- "This sentence is false."
This sentance...is false.
If true, then it is false.
If false, then it is true.
A loop.
A contradiction.
A poison.
Gold shaped his own version of such a wonder!
"The Living Origins are only alive because they are already dead."
HUUM!
A terrifying statement was made.
Contradicting!
Unfathomable!
And behind him, a golden Tower of Origin flickered- built to protect and to unravel.
To enforce contradiction!
The Living Origins roared with a shocked sense of despair.
White towers erupted from behind the Living Origins in response!
But...a heartbeat later, they began to crumble.
Altheon watched comrades unravel.
Shaynara screamed as she sought to hold on!
The faces of Origin turned to terror and disbelief as their essence cracked from within.
One Origin after another fell, their light snuffed by the unbearable contradiction of their own existence.
From the single statement filled with the complexity of Honored Gold!
An Honored Living Existence...was simply that powerful.
Only three remained.
Altheon.
Shaynara.
Vorellion.
And one more.
Bob.
The young one had not fallen in all this as one had to wonder...how?
Vorellion reeled from the massacre.
Its heads shook.
Each one dripping with sorrow!
It saw the perished Origins as it wanted to roar, but did not!
Then, with profound stillness, all nine heads turned to the sky.
"For my kin."
It did not roar.
It simply... gave.
And it gave everything with all its heart!
Origin surged.
The echoes of its purpose, the very reason for its birth, flared one last time.
And then...
"End!"
A pulse of Origin erupted as Vorellion unmade itself- from duty.
As a sacrifice.
In its unraveling, a flare was released.
A Call!
A summons for an Honored Living Origin.
Gold watched the act with distaste.
"Pathetic," he said.
His tone was dripping with disdain.
"Some things are best left to end.
There is peace in it.
A clean fade.
But you cling.
You flail."
He raised a hand.
"Let me clean it up."
He reached for Altheon, who braced himself!
But then...
Gold paused.
His hand froze in midair.
His eyes narrowed.
His Authority recoiled as his expression became heavy!
"Form the Transcendent Paradoxical Tower of Inevitability!" he bellowed.
The Fold fractured as what he sensed came down, a terrifying musing of Origin manifesting!
White light descended like thunder on silk.
An unmistakable brilliance.
A woman walked through the light.
Her legs emerged first, fair and radiant.
Then her dress, a flowing garment of sparkling white, stitched with stellar jewels.
Her hair, long and white, shimmered like the threads of destiny.
Her voice rang, clear and amused.
"Whatever could have pulled an Honored Living Paradox here?"
Gold’s expression soured as he sensed...
Royalty.
"Do the Living Origins have so many forces now that they send a Royal Living Origin to lesser Folds?"
The woman smiled.
"Royal Origin Calypso, at your service." she said sweetly, giving a curtsy no less regal for being unnecessary.
"And yes.
I came because someone here gave me good news about a little girl I thought dead"
Her gaze fell on Altheon.
"One of their bodies," she said, her voice soft as falling snow, "cannot perish."
And she smiled.
The Fold pulsed once more.
And the war reached a terrifying precipice!

chapters.title: Chapter 3912: Choices! III
paragraphs: Royal Origin Calypso stepped forward, the radiance of her form diffusing across the battlefield like a balm over open wounds.
Where her bare feet touched the twisted foldscape, the strands of reality shimmered, weaving themselves back together in gentle pulses of violet-gold light.
With a single flick of her finger, the decaying Origin of Vorellion was stilled. His unraveling ceased. The rhythm of his ancient purpose resumed, however feebly.
Her eyes swept across the field. Altheon. Shaynara. And Bob.
She lingered on the latter with the faintest spark of interest, then turned her gaze outward.
The battlefield was ruin. But not in the traditional sense of ash and flame. No, the deaths of Living Origins birthed a different kind of aftermath.

In their place stood crystallized echo-groves of trees with translucent leaves humming with fractured memory, roots that tangled through the fold beneath them, feeding on the echoes of unfinished beginnings.

White mist bled from them, curling into runes that could never be read twice the same way. And above each grove floated a single radiant sphere- the final beat of the Origin who had died, still pulsing in search of the purpose it was never allowed to complete!
Calypso exhaled a long breath. "What a bloody waste."

She looked up then, eyes falling upon Honored Gold, who remained elevated above the field, unmoved and unworried. Dozens of Living Paradoxes floated around him like silent stars in orbit. Their forms flickered in and out of clarity, their Authority humming together in deep synchrony.
Paradoxes had purposefully come together.
And what happened...when Paradoxes came together?!
Calypso whistled.
"I haven’t seen a Tower of Inevitability in a while. Did I really scare you that badly?"
WAA!

Honored Gold said nothing. He didn’t need to. His silence was a blade. Cold. Surgical. His aura, merged with the Prime and normal Paradoxes around him, pulsed in deliberate waves, each one drawing in paradoxical authority!
They were summoning it.
They wanted an Inevitability!
Calypso tilted her head, a smile playing at the edges of her lips.
"If I had come alone," she said sweetly, "this might have actually gotten troublesome."
She lifted one hand into the air and pointed up.
"Thankfully...I invited a friend."
The shift was immediate.
Honored Gold’s expression, previously etched in stone, cracked. His eyes flicked upward.
The Fold above them split open.
Out of the tear, a woman descended.

Or rather, she fell. Headfirst. Her body suspended upside down as though gravity had forgotten its place in the conversation. Long dark hair spilled out around her like unraveling ink across a blank page. Her skin was pale, flawless. Her features were delicate, almost too symmetrical to be natural, framed by the luminous white robe that hugged her form without ever actually touching her.
She smiled.
A bright, dangerous smile.
The aura she emanated struck silence into the battlefield.
Because it was not Living Origin Authority nor Living Paradoxical Authority!
It was...
Living Law!
A Living Law!
Unlike any other presence on the field, hers wasn’t oppressive through weight. It was clarity sharpened into a command- the promise that things would be as she declared.
She hovered midair, still upside down, spinning slowly as her eyes glinted with power.

"I was told a treasure of the Living Laws had ended up coming from this delightful little dump," she said. Her voice was light, lilting, far too amused. "Which was, if I’m not mistaken... your finding, Little Altheon?"
Altheon flinched and nodded.
The Living Law spun once more, flipping upright in the blink of an eye. Her smile deepened as she focused on Altheon.
"You give my dear Calypso here some good news- which she still refuses to share with me- and then send me a child repeating that he only wants peace from these folds. And yet..."
She opened her arms wide to the carnage.
"Here you are. In the middle of everything. Just what recent entanglements have you gotten yourself into, Altheon?"
Altheon offered no reply to such a question as he truly could not say much!
"My great friend," Calypso said, stepping beside her. "Royal Law Tristesse. Should we not address the... thing?"
She gestured up.
At the peak of Honored Gold’s golden Tower, something was emerging.
A Transcendent Inevitability.

Tentacles stretched out from the forming monstrosity- multicolored, pulsing with contradiction and hunger. Each tendril sang a note of entropy. The sound alone warped the space around it. The air bled. The folds frayed!
Tristesse glanced at it, then at Honored Gold.
"You Paradoxes never change. Always calling forth things you think you can contain."
"We are the ones most affected by Inevitabilities," Honored Gold replied. "You wouldn’t understand."
She shook her head.
"If you say so... you ugly fuck."
Her smile vanished.
In the next instant, her face turned fierce, and cold.
HUUM.
A silver tower erupted behind her.
Living Law Authority surged across the battlefield in the next moment!
"Living Paradoxical Authority," she declared, her voice reverberating as if etched directly into reality, "will not work in these folds for the next minute."
The moment the words left her lips, they became.
The folds accepted them.
Reality bent to follow.
Dozens of Living Paradoxes blinked in confusion. Their Authority dimmed. Their bodies flickered!
Above them, the Inevitability shrieked as it fully formed, its thousand tendrils unfurling like a flower of madness.
Tristesse looked down at them, her voice now a solemn melody.
"Little Paradoxes... do you know what Law is?"
She paused. Let silence fill the space.

"Law...is the formal expression of rational will. But here, it is more than that. It is a directive of purpose, not suggestion. It is reality’s spine, and I am its marrow. When I speak, existence recalibrates. When I declare, contradiction bows. That is Law."
She gazed down at the trembling Paradoxes.
"So... if I have laid down the law that you cannot use your Authority..."
Her eyes narrowed.
"How will you run from the Inevitability you called out yourselves?"
HUUM!
Panic erupted.
Paradoxes scattered. With no Authority to shield them, they fled with their bare existences, trying to escape the oncoming collapse.
Only Honored Gold remained still. Wings unfurled. Eyes burning.
He stared coldly into the growing chaos.
And above, the Inevitability screamed.
A thousand tentacles lashed out.
They devoured everything as just because it came from Living Paradoxes did not mean that it would not target them!
And amidst it all, in the eye of disorder, there was one who moved unseen.
Bob.
Quiet.
Solitary, and still.
He was....
Absorbing.
Drawing in the scattered remnants of the slain Living Origins.
And from within him, something unfathomable pulsed with glee as a shielded Inevitability cheered at the ongoing chaos!

chapters.title: Chapter 3913: Choices! IV
paragraphs: Royal Origin Calypso and Royal Law Tristesse floated side by side, their visages radiant with ancient power, exuding a splendor that bent the air around them.
Each emanated a sovereign presence- Calypso cloaked in regality, Tristesse in a calculated composure that never wavered.
Around them, existence itself groaned.
The Transcendent Inevitability raged.
Its tentacles lashed across reality, multicolored strands of hunger and ruin snapping and writhing.
Living Paradoxes- once draped in wings of contradiction and shimmering halos- tried to flee. But under the suffocating silence of Tristesse’s Law, their Authorities were nullified.
Powerless, many of them were caught!
HUUM!
The Inevitability devoured without pause.
Tentacles seized them mid-flight. Their radiant forms turned gray, dulling into husks as they were reeled back toward the central writhing mass. They had summoned it. And now, they were its feast!
Tristesse stood motionless, gaze locked onto the calamity.
"Calypso," she said, her voice smooth as it could be, "remind me again- how important are these folds?"
Calypso, every part of her frame exuding dignity, turned slowly. "What do you think?"
Her tone was cool, though her body radiated Living Origin Authority in steady, growing waves that pushed away the distant Inevitability.
"These are the folds that birthed a paradox that produces no Inevitabilities. Altheon found a Fold Dweller here in possession of something tied to the Living Laws and sent him to you. And..."
Her gaze deepened. "He also found something that...I am personally invested in. That’s three points. All tied to these Lesser Folds."

Tristesse allowed a small breath to leave her. Her eyes sharpened with clarity. "That’s enough then," she said, each word clipped with precision. "If I’m here, I might as well clean house. You didn’t bring me to dance around the issue...you brought me to isolate these folds, so I will!"
WAA!
Calypso inclined her head but said nothing. She turned, her jeweled robes gleaming like woven starlight. With unhurried grace, she surged toward the Inevitability- and Honored Gold.

"You there," she called, voice laced with honeyed malice, "weavings of contradiction and uncertainty. Ready to have your day utterly fucked?" Her eyes sparkled. "Do you think your Royal Living Paradoxes will execute you after today’s little failure? Or will the Inevitability devour you first?"
HUUM!
Without waiting, she plunged forward, an ocean of Origin descending!
Tristesse, behind her, exhaled and seated herself midair, crossing her legs with a deliberateness that echoed finality.
Altheon, standing nearby with Shaynara, Vorellion, and the silent Bob, blinked and asked softly, "Esteemed Miss... just what exactly are you doing?"
Tristesse smiled- calm, precise, and knowing. "Relocating these Folds," she said, her tone utterly rational. "From under the influence of Paradoxes. Into territory that obeys structure, and Law."
Then she lifted her chin.
"O Nullvein Gravewake Folds..."
Her voice deepened, becoming a resonant note that stretched across eternity.

"You were born in chaos, whispered into being by Paradox, raised beneath the shadow of ruin. But I see you. I see the strands that quiver beneath your skin. The laws you yearned for in silence. Now hear me. Obey me. Step forward. Out of contradiction, and into clarity! Come beneath the light of established Law! And be still. The Law...demands it!"
HUUM!
The Folds trembled.
From her body, silver light spilled out- an endless river of Law!
It raced across the distorted folds that were endless, chasing the broken latticework of paradox like ink over parchment. Everything shivered. Shifted!
A Law was laid down.
A Law was adopted.
A Law was followed!
Tristesse grimaced slightly, her brow twitching as strain lined her expression. But she did not falter.
She exhaled. "It’s been... a while," she murmured, wiping an invisible crease from her sleeve.
Altheon and the others said nothing.
And then...
A brilliant flash of silver bloomed.
The Nullvein Gravewake Folds...disappeared. Or really...displaced!
What remained behind was madness.
The Inevitability screeched. Honored Gold, undeterred, burst forward with Authority rekindled. He clashed against Calypso’s descent, the battlefield blooming with roaring contradiction.
BOOM!
She smiled as their powers collided. "I only needed to keep you distracted while my friend took everything from you."

Her voice dropped, her eyes gleaming. "Good luck, Honored Fuck. I will tell you that you and all other Living Paradoxes won’t be living quite so comfortably in the time to come...things are changing. And that change will be hard for Paradoxes to survive!"
WAA!
She vanished.
Behind her, Paradoxes scrambled. The Inevitability unfurled more limbs, snatching bodies and fracturing logic.
Only Honored Gold remained unshaken. He stood amidst ruin, his voice low, cold, deliberate.

"It is not Paradoxes who will know discomfort in the days to come." His golden eyes narrowed. "It is all of you. None of you... are prepared. For the Paradox that cannot produce Inevitabilities. For Diviticus!"
Paradoxical Authority surged outward like a sea as he turned to meet the thing he had summoned!
Elsewhere.
A new weaving of existence...but also not.
WAP!
Royal Origin Calypso appeared amidst folds that were unraveling like coiled nightmares.
But there was...a semblance of Law now. A silver light seeped through them- cool, deliberate, and orderly!
What once was chaos became silence.
Around her, the silver brilliance blanketed everything. The Nullvein Gravewake Folds had been moved.
Tristesse stood at the center, composed, radiant. Altheon, Vorellion, Bob, and Shaynara nearby.
Calypso’s voice was like a heavgly blade. "You should have sent these folds into the care of the Living Origins. Not into the domains of the Living Laws."
Tristesse met her gaze with even calm and smiled.

"We’re allies, aren’t we?" she asked, "What matters is not whose territory they fall under. What matters is that Paradoxes will have a harder time reaching them now. And we’ll have time to understand... why these folds drew such attention."
Calypso said nothing. But her eyes glinted.
Then she turned.
Her gaze fell upon Altheon. "You. Come."
Altheon moved without hesitation, her Authority wrapping around them both.
As they moved away, her voice dropped. "Tell me. Has the Young Miss arrived yet in the Transcendent Origin Battlefront Folds?"
Altheon hesitated. Then nodded. "Soon," he said.
He paused again. "Though she is... not alone. She’s accompanied by a Fold Dweller."
Calypso stopped.
Altheon’s eyes met hers.
"Someone known as...Noah Osmont."

Calypso’s voice was like a heavgly blade.
"You should have sent these folds into the care of the Living Origins.
Not into the domains of the Living Laws."
Tristesse met her gaze with even calm and smiled.
"We’re allies, aren’t we?" she asked, "What matters is not whose territory they fall under.
What matters is that Paradoxes will have a harder time reaching them now.
And we’ll have time to understand... why these folds drew such attention."
Calypso said nothing.
But her eyes glinted.
Then she turned.
Her gaze fell upon Altheon.
"You.
Come."
Altheon moved without hesitation, her Authority wrapping around them both.
As they moved away, her voice dropped.
"Tell me.
Has the Young Miss arrived yet in the Transcendent Origin Battlefront Folds?"
Altheon hesitated.
Then nodded.
"Soon," he said.
He paused again.
"Though she is... not alone.
She’s accompanied by a Fold Dweller."
Calypso stopped.
Altheon’s eyes met hers.
"Someone known as...Noah Osmont."

chapters.title: Chapter 3914: Choices! V
paragraphs: The air held pulsed with glory!
Royal Origin Calypso raised her brows as she asked.
"For you to mention him, is he something to worry about?"
Altheon’s eyes flashed with uniqueness as he seemed to deliberate something...and he then he shook his head.
He remembered the words of the Young Miss!
And so...he made a choice.
Like all others, he made a choice!
"No, she had locked away her weavings, and this Osmont is merely an attendant of hers that protected her, so I decided to reward him by keeping him close, and the Young Miss also allowed it."
Calypso nodded at these words as she did not give them too much weight.
She looked out across the Nullvein Gravewake Folds that were nowin a different place as she voiced out...
"We have much to do. Honor those fallen and we shall have many more Origins scour these folds, and I will make preparations for the Young Miss."
The Nullvein Gravewake Folds were no longer what they once were!
Displaced, restructured, retethered.
The silver luster of Living Law Authority bled through its every strand, a quiet verdict passed across an entire dominion of collapse.
What once trembled with contradiction and unformed potential now pulsed with structure, boundary, and definition.
The mists that once refused to part were unweaving themselves into paths- mapped and measured, no longer shrouded in aimless paradox!
It was an overwhelming presence. Regal. Final. And terrifying in the way all certainty could be!
The figures of Living Origins moved through it now, their radiant authority mingling with the silver streams of Living Law.
In these very same folds.
Far away, at the heart of the Infiniverse Wheel of Existence that was hidden from the eyes of even Living Existences!
On golden sands that pulsed with ancient possibility, the Early Veiled Shore remained untouched.
Noah Osmont sat barefoot, his arms resting over his knees, looking out across the glimmering tide as his body continued to be surrounded by multicolored waves of complexity.
The horizon of the Folds shimmered with silver threads- ghostly reflections of the very beings that sought him. Calypso. Altheon. Tristesse.
He had observed how the entire battle between them and the Living Paradoxes had unfolded, all the way to this point!
He smiled softly.
"Choices, choices," he said.

Behind him, the sound of splashing water echoed. Moiraine emerged, her steps silent as she carried a crystalline container holding twenty shimmering Schrödinger’s Boxes, each holding a trembling marine lifeform bound by the earliest weavings of existence.
"You made quick work of them," he remarked.
Moiraine gave a nod of awe as her body also buzzed with rising complexity.
"I did as you commanded, Sir."
"..." Noah’s gaze lingered on the horizon.
The Folds had changed...not because of overwhelming force.
They changed because the Paradoxes failed to prepare for nuance! They were caught off guard by involvement they didn’t account for or know about!
Sigrid.
And a treasure of Living Laws that was found in these folds.
His fingers brushed over his chest, over the place where his power was continuing to bloom as another part of the Heart of an Early Creature would soon begin to form.
Two of the reasons that brought Royal Living Existences here... were related to him.
Sigrid, and the Paradox that did not produce Inevitabilities!
The third related to Living Laws he was curious about, but...
He turned his gaze to the glowing bucket beside him, its golden liquid- the Sacred Mead of Existence, shimmering like a dream made tangible.
Near it, Heidrun lay basking beneath the Sacred Totem of Infinity, her glowing fur bathed in warm celestial hues as her arrogant eyes looked content.
The Veiled Shore of an Early Creature was a place of unfathomable possibilities.
His hand hovered over the sands, and in his mind, he wondered. Could he now challenge the Record of an Early Creature?
Could he elevate the Budding Shore?!
Such a question rose as another body of his...was continuing entanglements elsewhere!
Elsewhere.

Across a channel carved between the Living Origin Labyrinth and the Transcendent Origin Battlefront Folds, rivers of white gold bent and curved endlessly- a place where direction folded upon itself and momentum was heavy!
Within one of these drifting streams, Noah and Sigrid floated side by side.
She had been talking- quiet, almost playful- about the Story of the Earliest Folds. Her voice had been confident, regal, her tone rich with what she knew.
And then she stopped.
Her body stilled as her head turned toward him sharply.
Without a word, her hands moved. A veil of white gold brilliance wrapped around them, sealing them from the ever-listening gaze of Altheon that should have been monitoring them here!

She stood in front of him then, wrapped in a flowing white robe that clung gloriously to her form. Her pale hair, split with streaks of obsidian, framed her calculating face that was no longer playful, but wary. The runic tattoos on her skin shimmered beneath the robe, burning dimly with muted authority.
"I think... I’m in trouble," she whispered.
Noah’s eyes sharpened. "Oh?"
Her lips twisted as she breathed out, looking deeply into his eyes.
"I was meant to become the Living Order," she began, her voice low and steady. "Something I didn’t ask for. Something I hate because of all ther sacrifices made."
Her breath quickened , though her tone stayed cool.

"But now... now I’m bound to you. And you’ve been marked by me. And just now, my entire existence just shuddered from sensing you. On the other side of that bond. You feel... enormous. Impossibly enormous."
Her words slipped out, as though she did not entirely want to know the answer to the question she was asking.
Yet she had to ask!
"Just who are you, really?"
HUUM!
Noah’s voice was heavy.
"Do you really want to know?"
Sigrid bit her lip.
She nodded once.
He lifted his hand.
She hesitated.
Then stepped forward, placing her hand into his.
His aura flowed into her like heavy gravity. It pulled at the deepest parts of her being as she began to feel...euphoria!
Her eyes trembled.
Noah’s voice was quiet.
"What beings did Living Existences look up to? Revere?"
Her expression faltered. Her mind moved rapidly as everything lined up! She half knew it. She thought it. But to confirm it...!
HUUM!
She whispered, her stellar eyes wide.
"I really am in a lot of trouble..."
